Connectors are connected with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect.`, before the agent or any row is checked, and nothing is saved. `fieldstatus` is ignored if sent; the server assigns it. Wiro-managed (`platform`) fields are rejected (`<Field label> is managed by the platform`). All fields are validated first; one invalid field rejects the whole request (`result: false`, nothing saved). If a save fails after validation, the other fields stay saved (`result: false`, `applied` counts the saved ones). Whitespace around text, password, email, URL and number values (and around each string-list entry) is trimmed before validation and saving; inner spaces stay, and multi-line text, selections, booleans, files and nested rows are saved as sent. A starting or running agent restarts when a saved value changes. A secret sent as "••••••••" (the mask Detail shows, spaces around it ignored) keeps the saved value: it isn't written, isn't counted in `applied` and restarts nothing; the mask with other text beside it is refused and nothing is saved.
POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind: `{ useragentguid, projectid? }` → `{ result, errors, applied, project: { id, name }, restart }`. Saves the project's API key as the agent's Wiro project (`credentials.wiro.apikey`), which pays for the models its skills run. `projectid` is a project's `id` from `POST /Project/List` (`{}`: the projects of the calling workspace, newest first, up to 100); a request made with a project API key may leave it out to bind that key's own project, and any other request must send it. `applied`: 1 when the saved key changed, 0 when the agent already had this project. `restart`: `scheduled` (starting or running, now restarts with the key), `none` (nothing changed, or not running and uses the key at its next start) or `failed` (the key is saved; stop and start the agent to load it). Binding doesn't change `status`: an agent at status 6 (Setup Required) has no plan; pay it with `CreateSubscriptionCheckout` (`useprepaid: true`), which queues it. Access: the agent's owner or a team admin of its team (plain members get code 97, others 96, unknown or deleted agents 95). The request's workspace must be the agent's. The project must be too: a personal agent takes one of its owner's personal projects, a team agent a project of its team (a team admin any of them, the member who deployed it the ones they created). Refusals: `projectid is required: send the id of one of your projects from Project/List. Only a request made with a project API key may leave it out, to bind that key's own project.`, `projectid must be a project's id from Project/List.`, `Project not found. Send the id of one of your projects from Project/List: one you created, or any project of a team you are an admin of.`, `This is a personal agent: bind one of its owner's personal projects. Its model runs are paid from that wallet.`, `This is a team agent: bind one of its team's projects. Its model runs are paid from the team wallet.`, `This project's API key no longer works: the account that created it is not active, so the agent's model runs would fail. Bind another project.`, `This project's API key no longer works: the person who created it is no longer in the team, so the agent's model runs would fail. Bind another project of the team.`, `The project could not be bound. Try again.`
POST /UserAgent/CredentialFileUpload: multipart `{ useragentguid, credentialkey, fieldname, file }` → `{ result, url, credentialkey, fieldname }`. For credential schema fields whose `type` is `"fileinput"` only (a stored file reference): only the `holdaudio` and `holdmusic` fields of Twilio Voice (`twilio-voice`). A connector's key file (a Google service account JSON, an App Store Connect private key) is not a credential: send its contents in `values` on `POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect`; a connector's slug sent here as `credentialkey` answers `Unknown credential: <key>`, and a field of another type `Field is not a fileinput type`. Validates mimetype against `filetypes[]` and size against `maxsize` (KB; default cap 10240 KB / 10 MB). The agent restarts to apply the change.
POST /UserAgent/CredentialFieldHistory: `{ useragentguid, credentialkey, startdate?, enddate? }` → `{ result, entries }`. Newest first, up to 500: each entry is a value a save replaced (`operation: "update"`, with `changedby` and `changedat`); a first save adds none, and neither does a list sent whole (Telegram `groups`, Slack `channels`, Discord `guilds`, website `urls`). A list value comes back as its stored JSON text. A secret's earlier value reads `"[REDACTED]"`; Wiro-managed credentials return an empty `entries`.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillUpsert: `{ useragentguid, skillkey, value?, interval?, enabled?, description? }` → `{ result, restarting }`. Server auto-normalises skillkey to canonical `cs-*` / `cs-cron-*` based on `interval` presence (or explicit prefix); `cron-<slug>` becomes `cs-cron-<slug>` with or without `interval`. `usercreated` is server-managed: a newly created skill gets `true`, and an update keeps the skill's current value. `enabled` is writable for BOTH strategies (`cs-*`) and crons (`cs-cron-*`). A disabled strategy is suppressed end-to-end (it still appears in the list, but the agent never loads it). `interval` only persists on `cs-cron-*` rows. `description` is only persisted on user-created rows; a preset row's description is template-owned: sending it back unchanged is ignored, a different text is rejected with `customskill-preset-description-not-editable`. A `value` or `description` edit of an existing skill reaches a running agent without a restart (`restarting: false`); a new skill or task, a new `interval`, an `enabled` change or any change to `cs-approval-policy` restarts a starting or running agent (`restarting: true`), and so does a text edit the running agent can't take. A scheduled task's `interval` must be a cron expression the agent can run (five fields: minute hour day month weekday) on a date that comes: otherwise nothing is saved and the error says what is wrong and what to write, e.g. `This schedule can't run. The hour field takes 0 to 23. A schedule has five fields: minute hour day month weekday, for example 0 9 * * 1-5.` or, for `0 0 30 2 *`, `This schedule never comes up: February has no 30th. Pick a day February has, such as 28.` Only a schedule sent in the request is checked. A task runs only while its gates are open (one of its `requires_connectors` connected, one of its `requires_credentials` set up, a Skill that brings it on); `enabled: true` doesn't lift them, and CustomSkillUpsert takes neither list. Saving or clearing a credential sets `enabled` on every custom skill and scheduled task whose `requires_credentials` names it. On a template agent, a scheduled task the template brings runs the template's text: a `value` sent for it is saved and shown on Detail, but the agent doesn't use it.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillRename: `{ useragentguid, oldskillkey, newskillkey, description? }` → `{ result, newskillkey }`. User-created rows only (`usercreated: true`). Flavour preserved: `cs-cron-*` ↔ `cs-*` rejected with `Scheduled tasks and custom skills cannot be renamed into each other — delete the row and re-create it with the right kind`. Preset rows are refused with `Preset skills cannot be renamed.` Collision → `A skill with that key already exists for this agent`; same key → `The new skill key is the same as the current one — nothing to rename`; unknown old key → `Skill not found`. Version history moves to the new key and a `rename` audit entry is appended. The agent restarts to apply the change.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillAlternatives: `{ useragentguid, skillkey }` → `{ result, alternatives: [{ title, description, value, intervalexpr? }] }`. Read-only template list for the panel's "Browse alternatives" picker; apply via `CustomSkillUpsert` on the SAME `skillkey` (alternatives don't carry their own `key` and are addressed by index). `intervalexpr` only present on cron-flavoured alternatives. Empty `alternatives[]` is a success.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillDelete: `{ useragentguid, skillkey }` → `{ result }`. User-created rows only, and the delete removes the skill's version history too. A row with `usercreated: false` (a template's skills and tasks copied at deploy, a custom build's registry rows such as `cs-approval-policy` and bundled `cs-cron-*` tasks) is refused with code 0 `This skill is registry-owned and cannot be deleted. Use enabled=false to disable it instead.`, and a user-created row under a key the template also has with `This skill belongs to the agent preset and cannot be deleted. Use enabled=false to disable it instead.`, both with `suggestion: "disable-via-upsert"`. A key the agent doesn't have deletes nothing and answers `result: true`.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillHistory: `{ useragentguid, skillkey, startdate?, enddate? }` → `{ result, entries, preset_default }`. One entry per change, holding the state before it (creating a skill adds none); `operation` is `update-user`, `rename`, `revert-to-history`, `reset-to-preset`, `clone-deploy`, `seed-custom-build`, `insert-cascade`, `update-cascade` or `delete-cascade`.
POST /UserAgent/CustomSkillRevert: `{ useragentguid, skillkey, source: "preset"|"history", versionguid? }` → `{ result, action, current_value, current_interval, current_enabled }`; `action` is `reverted`, `re-inserted`, `reset`, `deleted` or `no-op`.
POST /UserAgent/SkillsApply: `{ useragentguid, skills: { "util-skillname": bool }, tier?, idempotencyKey }` → `{ result, tier, restartTriggered, restartedAt, stripeProrationApplied: false, prepaidWalletDelta: null, usedCreditsUsd: 0, pricing: { enabledSkills, delta: 0, deltaUsd: 0, ... } }` (the rest of `pricing` repeats the plan's unchanged price for older clients). Never charges or refunds anything: every plan includes every skill, so the plan's price and included AI usage stay the same, and no active plan is needed. `tier` is only for older clients: a value other than the agent's current plan is refused with `Change the plan with UpgradeTier.` **No-op short-circuit:** when every entry in `skills` already matches the persisted state, the response is `{result:true, errors:[], noOp:true}` with no other fields populated: no DB write, no restart. Treat `noOp:true` as the signal to skip your own post-apply UI churn. The ONLY skill-toggle endpoint API consumers should use. Even single-skill toggles go through this. Atomic batch with one restart, idempotent. Works on template deploys too: a skill the agent changes overrides its template for that skill only, and later template updates still reach every skill it never changed. Only the agent's owner or a team admin may call it (plain members: 97). `skills` takes Skills (`util-*`) only. A Skill turned on needs its `depends_on` Skills, and theirs, on already or in the same map; SkillsApply turns none on. The same key with the same skills within 10 minutes returns the first answer, and with other skills it is refused with 107. After that, the key of a change that was applied gets 107 when the call would change something, and `noOp: true` when it changes nothing. Error codes: 0 `Unknown skill: <names>` (not a Skill, such as an `int-` name; nothing changed), 101 `Cannot apply: some skills require other skills to be enabled.` (with `deps[]`), 102 `Cannot apply: some skills conflict with each other.` (with `conflicts[]`), 104 `A skill update is already in progress for this agent — please retry shortly.` (another skill or plan change is running), 105 `Change the plan with UpgradeTier.` (a `tier` other than the agent's current plan; nothing is changed), 107 `This idempotencyKey was already used for a different skill change. Nothing was changed; send a new idempotencyKey.` / `This idempotencyKey was already used for an earlier skill change. Nothing was changed; send a new idempotencyKey.` / `Cached response corrupt — please retry with a new idempotency key.`, 108 `Failed to apply skill changes — please retry.`
POST /UserAgent/PricingPreview: two body shapes, (a) draft `{ draft: true, tier?, skills: [...] }` for Builder; (b) existing `{ useragentguid, tier?, skillOverrides?, withScheduledTasks? }`. `tier` defaults to the plan the agent's renewal bills (a scheduled lower plan, else its own; Starter in a draft), and a value that names no plan is ignored. Returns `{ tier, totalPriceUsd, tokenRates, skillBreakdown[] (each `{ skill, priceUsd: 0, billing_model: "tokens" }`), enabledSkills, directSkills, tiers: { starter, pro, max }, planChange? }`. `totalPriceUsd` is the previewed plan's price, also the AI usage it includes a month; skills never change it. Also `plans` (the three plans with names, prices, `includedUsageUsd` and `diskMb`) and, for an existing agent, `nextplan` (a lower plan already scheduled for its renewal, or null). `planChange` (existing agent with an active plan, else null): `{ change: "upgrade"|"downgrade"|"none", provider: "prepaid", fromTier, toTier, nextplan, priceUsd, effectiveAt, newPeriod: false, periodEnd, secondsLeft, chargeNowUsd }`. An upgrade shows what it costs now (at list price before any discount: the prorated difference, paid from the balance, effective now; the period's included AI usage grows by the same difference for the time left); a downgrade starts at `effectiveAt` = `periodEnd` (`chargeNowUsd` 0); "none" (the agent's own plan, or a skill-only preview) shows no charge. Its credit counts (`totalMonthlyCredits`, `credits`, `monthlyCredits`, `creditsNow`, `creditsThisPeriod`, `creditsFromRenewal`) are deprecated. With `withScheduledTasks: true` (body b) it also returns `scheduledTasks: { stop: string[], resume: string[] }`, the scheduled task keys the skillOverrides would stop and start (empty lists without skillOverrides; null when it could not be worked out).
POST /UserAgent/CreateSubscriptionCheckout: `{ useragentguid, useprepaid: true, tier?: "starter"|"pro"|"max" }` → `{ result, subscriptionId, tier, monthlypriceusd, chargedUsd }`. `tier` defaults to the agent's own plan; a value that names no plan is refused with `tier must be starter, pro or max`. Always pass useprepaid: true: the plan is paid from the Wiro balance (a short balance: code 97 with `neededusd`); without it, the retired card checkout answers `result: false`, `retired: true`, `Agent plans are paid from your Wiro balance. Add funds, then choose the plan.` and charges nothing. Rejects if useragent already has an active subscription. Code 104 `Another payment from this wallet is still going through. Nothing was charged; please try again in a minute.` while another plan payment from the same wallet is going through; `We couldn't confirm this agent's previous checkout. Please try again in a minute.` when Wiro can't confirm the agent's plan or an earlier checkout (nothing charged).
POST /UserAgent/Start: `{ guid }` → Queues agent (status 2). Needs an active plan first: without one it answers code 97 with `agentusage` (`pausedreason: "plan"`) and `<agent> has no active plan. Choose a plan to keep it running.` (renew a plan that ended with `RenewSubscription`; an agent that never had one starts one with `CreateSubscriptionCheckout` and `useprepaid: true`), whatever the balance. Then it needs included AI usage left or a balance of at least $0.50, else code 97 with the Send refusal's message and `agentusage`; a plain member of a team agent's team gets code 97 `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.` with no `agentusage`.
POST /UserAgent/Stop: `{ guid }` → Stops or moves to Stopping.
POST /UserAgent/Delete: `{ useragentguid }` (or `guid`) → `{ result, useragent: { guid, deletedat } }`. Soft-delete: `deletedat` is stamped and returned and the agent is unpinned; Delete itself doesn't erase its history (transactions, credential and custom-skill change history, messages). The agent's working files (its memory and the files it saved) are kept 30 days after the delete, then removed for good; media it sent in chat is stored separately and stays. The agent is then excluded from Detail, MyAgents, Start, Stop, the agent runtime and its scheduled jobs, and TransactionList, CredentialFieldHistory, CustomSkillHistory, Logs, LogsList, LogsFile, LogsDelete, RunStreamToken, Message/History, Message/Sessions, Message/DeleteSession, Message/RenameSession and Message/Delete return `useragent-not-found` (95) for it, so export what you need first. Requires status `0`/`5`/`6` (running rejected with `Stop the agent before deleting it.`; `5` passes only once the agent no longer holds its runtime, otherwise the same error: call Stop and wait for `0`) and no active subscription that CancelSubscription hasn't set to end (`Cancel the agent's subscription before deleting it.`; once CancelSubscription has set a balance-paid plan to end, the agent can be deleted right away, the rest of the period is forfeited with no refund and the plan ends at `cancelsAt`; a plan paid by card before the move to the balance blocks until `cancelsAt`, so retry once it has expired). Owner or team admin only (others: `User agent not found` 95, `You don't have access to this user agent` 96, `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.` 97). A repeat call on an already-deleted agent returns `User agent not found` (95); treat that as already deleted. The stored `deletedat` never changes.
POST /UserAgent/Pin: `{ useragentguid, pinned }` → `{ result }`. `pinned` is a flag on the agent: on a team agent any team member can set it, and every member's PinnedAgents shows it.
POST /UserAgent/PinnedAgents: `{}` (scoped to the API key's workspace) → `{ result, useragents }`.
POST /UserAgent/PinnedUnread: `{}` → `{ result, data: [{ useragentguid, lastmessageguid }] }`.
POST /UserAgent/CreateExtraCreditCheckout: retired. Answers `{ result: false, retired: true, url: null, errors: [{ message: "Extra credit packs are retired. Your agent uses your Wiro balance after its plan's included usage. Add funds to your balance instead." }] }` and charges nothing. While another plan payment from the same wallet is going through, Deploy and CreateSubscriptionCheckout with `useprepaid: true` and RenewSubscription answer `Another payment from this wallet is still going through. Nothing was charged; please try again in a minute.`
POST /UserAgent/CancelSubscription: `{ guid }` → `{ result, cancelsAt }`. Cancel at period end (`cancelsAt`: a day after `currentperiodend` for a balance-paid plan, the period end for a card plan), reverse with RenewSubscription (no charge). A scheduled lower plan stays (`nextplan` keeps it): once the plan ends, the agent shows that plan and its price (`tier`, `monthlypriceusd`, `nextplan: null`), which RenewSubscription charges; the undo keeps it, and UpgradeTier with the current plan drops it. A card plan's cancel drops it (`nextplan` back to null). It works on a plan paid by card too (the owner, or on a team agent a team admin or the organization owner), also one set to switch to the balance: the switch is dropped and the plan ends at its period end (`pendingdowngrade: "cancel"`), nothing charged or refunded; RenewSubscription undoes it and restores the switch.
POST /UserAgent/UpgradeTier: `{ guid, targetTier: "starter"|"pro"|"max", allowDowngrade?: true }` → `{ result, change: "upgrade"|"downgrade"|"downgrade-cancelled", tier, previousTier, targetTier, nextplan, effectiveAt, ... }`. An upgrade adds `newPriceUsd, periodEnd, chargedUsd, proratedCharge`: the Wiro balance pays the prorated difference now (a short balance answers code 97 with `neededusd` and nothing changes), the period's included AI usage grows by the difference for the time left, and every renewal includes the new plan in full. A plan paid by card before plans moved to the balance is upgraded the same way, from the balance. A downgrade needs `allowDowngrade: true`; without it a lower `targetTier` answers `The <Plan> plan is smaller than this agent's <Plan> plan, so this is not an upgrade. Nothing was changed. A move to a smaller plan starts at the next renewal; to ask for it, send allowDowngrade: true.` With `allowDowngrade: true`, a higher `targetTier` answers `This agent is on the <Plan> plan now, so <Plan> is an upgrade. Nothing was changed. Reload the plan and ask again.` and nothing is changed or charged. A downgrade returns `nextplan`, `startsAt` (= `effectiveAt`, the renewal), `newPriceUsd` and `periodEnd`: no charge or refund. The agent's current plan cancels a scheduled downgrade (`downgrade-cancelled`, `nextplan: null`, `effectiveAt` now, `periodEnd`); an agent still on a price from before the three plans gets its current plan scheduled instead (`nextplan` = its plan, with `startsAt` and `newPriceUsd` for the renewal that moves it to that plan's price). With nothing scheduled it answers `Already on the <Plan> plan.` A bad `targetTier` answers `targetTier must be starter, pro or max`; no active plan answers `No active plan. Use /UserAgent/CreateSubscriptionCheckout with useprepaid: true to start one on the plan you pick.`; on a plan paid by card, one set to end answers `This plan is set to end when its period ends, so it cannot be changed. Renew it first: it then renews from your balance.`, a scheduled lower plan that already started answers `The move to the <Plan> plan started with this billing period, and its payment moves the agent there, so it can no longer be undone. …`, and card billing that can't be read answers `We couldn't read this plan's billing. Nothing was changed; please try again in a minute.` Code 104 with `Another change to this agent's plan is going through. Nothing was changed; please try again in a minute.` while a skill change or another plan change of the agent is going through, or `Another payment from this wallet is still going through. Nothing was charged; please try again in a minute.` while another payment from the same wallet is; nothing is charged.
POST /UserAgent/RenewSubscription: `{ guid }` → either `{ action: "undo-cancel" }` (no charge; a plan paid by card goes back to switching to the balance) or `{ action: "renewed", plan: "agent", tier, amount, chargedUsd }` (the Wiro balance charged the plan's price, `chargedUsd` what it paid after a user or team discount, from the owner's wallet or the team's, expired sub rolled forward into a fresh 30-day active period; agents in status 0/5 are auto-queued back to 2). A renewal charges the plan's price and includes its AI usage in full; a scheduled `nextplan` applies at that renewal and is cleared. A short balance answers code 97 `Your balance is $x; this plan needs $y. Add funds to continue.` with `neededusd`; another plan payment from the same wallet answers code 104 `Another payment from this wallet is still going through. Nothing was charged; please try again in a minute.`; a plan paid by card that already switches to the balance answers `Subscription is already active. It renews from your balance when its period ends.`; and `We couldn't confirm this agent's previous checkout. Please try again in a minute.` means nothing was charged. An ended plan shows the plan and price its renewal takes (`tier`, `monthlypriceusd`, `nextplan: null`), and a renewal never charges more than `monthlypriceusd` shows: when it would, nothing is charged, the agent is set to show the renewal's plan and price, and the call answers `This plan now renews on the <Plan> plan at $<price> a month, not the $<shown> it showed. Nothing was charged. Renew again to pay the new price.` A renewal whose plan could not be saved after the wallet paid answers code 110, `The wallet was charged $X.XX, but the renewal did not finish. Please contact support and do not try again.`: never retry it (Deploy and CreateSubscriptionCheckout with useprepaid answer code 110 with `... but the plan could not be saved. ...`, UpgradeTier with `... but the plan change did not finish. ...`).
POST /UserAgent/TransactionList: `{ useragentguid, kind?: "all"|"ai-usage"|"model-run"|"plan"|"funds", limit?, start? }` → `{ result, kind, rowstotal, summary, rows }`, newest first. rows: the agent's rows of the ledger of the wallet that pays for it now (the team wallet for a team agent, else its owner's; after a move to another workspace, the rows the earlier wallet holds are listed only in that wallet's Wallet/TransactionList): AI usage, covered by the plan or paid from the balance; the model runs it started; plan payments; funds added from its page; and, from before dollar billing, its older usage and plan records converted to dollars (`legacy: true`; card renewals of a plan paid by card are always legacy rows). Each row: `{ id, createdat, kind: "ai-usage"|"model-run"|"plan"|"funds"|"other", title, description, model (ai-usage rows: the costliest call's model; `tokens` and `costs` add up all its calls), tokens: { input, cacheRead, cacheWrite, output }, costs (ai-usage rows: USD per kind, exact to 7 decimals), amountusd (whole cents; when Wiro measures the agent's model calls itself a fraction of a cent carries to the next row, otherwise each turn is billed at its exact cost rounded up to the next cent; null only on a legacy plan row whose record kept no payment), paidfrom: "plan"|"balance"|"coupon"|"card"|null, direction: "out" (spending and refunds)|"in" (funds added and other credits), surface, taskid, legacy }`. A legacy `plan` row is a payment like any other: `direction: "out"`, its `amountusd` is what was paid (null when the old record kept no payment, never the AI usage the payment granted) and its `title` names the plan (`Agent renewal: Pro plan`, `Agent plan started: Starter plan`, `Agent plan change: Starter to Pro`; a record that names no plan keeps its own line); a refund taken back from pack money moved to the balance is a `funds` row titled `Refund` with `direction: "out"` (its `description` starts with `Refund:`). rowstotal: every row the kind lists, rows from before dollar billing included, for every kind; `kind: "plan"` lists every plan payment, legacy ones included. summary (this calendar month, UTC): `{ month, planusd, aiusageplanusd, aiusagebalanceusd, modelrunsusd, fundsaddedusd (from its page and pack money moved to the balance, less refunds taken back from it), includedusd, usage (as on Detail; its `resetsat` is the end of the active plan's period, null when the agent has no active plan) }`; a field is null when it could not be read (ask again). AI usage the plan covers changes no balance: the plan payment paid for it. Errors: `Request parameter [useragentguid] required` (0), `User agent not found` (95; also a deleted agent), `You don't have access to this user agent` (96), `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.` (97, a team member who is not a team admin), HTTP 401 for a missing or invalid API key; `Failed to load transactions — please retry.` (0) is a failed read: retry, it is never an empty list. The old `transactions`, `total` and credit summary fields are deprecated and will be removed. A plan start or renewal the wallet paid but whose plan could not be saved (code 110, or Wiro's own renewal) is a `plan` row like any other; the agent's `AGENT_PLAN_NOT_SAVED` activity row tells it apart (after Wiro's own renewal ends this way RenewSubscription answers `Subscription is already active`), and one from before dollar billing is a legacy `other` row with `amountusd` 0.
POST /UserAgent/Logs: `{ useragentguid, date?, lines? }` → `{ result, date, totalLines, events }`. Live tail. Poll every 30 seconds or more. `totalLines` is the row count for the day, who-did-what rows and notes included (not the page size). Events are NEWEST-FIRST (descending by `ts`). Each event: `{ ts: ISO-8601 string, kind, tool?, toolintegration?, toolaction?, title, summary?, durationMs?, ok?, error?, userUuid?, user? }`. `kind` values: `turn_started`, `turn_ended`, `tool_started`, `tool_completed`, `tool_blocked`, `cron_finished`, `user_message` (Telegram/Slack/Discord messages only), `token_usage`, `token_usage_idempotent`, `media_relay`, `background_reply`. A `turn_ended` for a turn the caller cancelled has no `ok`, and its title reads `Agent turn cancelled`. A `cron_finished` for a Scheduled Task run that was paused has no `ok` either: its title starts with `Paused without an active plan:` (the agent has no active plan), else `Paused by a spend limit:` (the agent's spend limit is reached), else `Paused by a Model Access rule:` (its rule blocks the task's model), and its `summary` is `{ jobId, status: "paused", reason: "plan"|"spend_limit"|"model_access" }`. Additive who-did-what kinds, each with `title`, `ok: true`, `summary?` and who did it: `AGENT_STARTED`, `AGENT_STOPPED`, `AGENT_RESTARTED`, `AGENT_RENAMED`, `AGENT_UPDATED`, `AGENT_SETTINGS_UPDATED`, `AGENT_TRANSFERRED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_ADDED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_UPDATED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_RENAMED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_DELETED`, `AGENT_INSTRUCTION_REVERTED`, `AGENT_SKILLS_UPDATED`, `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_SAVED` (`Setting saved: <credential>.<field>`, or `Settings saved: …` for several: a channel, the agent's Wiro project or another setting; connecting a connector writes `CONNECTOR_CONNECTED`), `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_REVEALED` (`Setting revealed: <credential>.<field>`, when someone showed a saved key in full in the Wiro panel; never the key itself), `AGENT_CREDENTIAL_REMOVED` (`Disconnected: wiro`, when the agent's Wiro project was disconnected because the agent moved to a workspace the project isn't in, or because the project's team or organization was deleted), `CONNECTOR_CONNECTED` (`Connector connected: <slug>`), `CONNECTOR_DISCONNECTED` (`Connector disconnected: <slug>`; `Connector disconnected: wiro` with `summary.reason: "workspace"` when the agent moved to a workspace its Wiro project isn't in, or its Wiro project's team or organization was deleted), `CONNECTOR_ACCOUNTS_SET` (`Connector accounts set: <slug>`), `CONNECTOR_REAUTH` (`Connector needs to be connected again: <slug>`, written by Wiro when a sign-in expired or was revoked), `AGENT_PLAN_STARTED`, `AGENT_PLAN_RENEWED`, `AGENT_PLAN_CANCELLED`, `AGENT_PLAN_RESUMED`, `AGENT_PLAN_NOT_SAVED` (`Pro plan renewal did not finish: $24.00 charged`, `Max plan start did not finish: $100.00 charged`: the balance paid and the plan could not be saved), `AGENT_PLAN_ENDED` (`<Plan> plan ended: <why>`, such as `Starter plan ended: the wallet could not pay the renewal` or `Pro plan ended: it was set to cancel`; written by Wiro, and the agent stops when its plan ends), `AGENT_PLAN_CHANGE_SCHEDULED`, `AGENT_PLAN_CHANGE_CANCELLED`, `AGENT_PLAN_MOVE_SCHEDULED`, `AGENT_TIER_UPGRADED`, `AGENT_CREDITS_PURCHASED` and `AGENT_CHECKOUT_CREATED` (older rows only: a pack bought before packs were retired, and a card checkout link from before plans moved to the balance), `AGENT_LOG_DAY_DELETED`, `AGENT_SCREEN_VIEWED` (at most one per person and agent an hour), `AGENT_SCREEN_CONTROLLED` (at most one per person and agent every 10 minutes), `AGENT_SCREEN_CONTROL_ENDED` (one per Take Control session; `summary: { seconds, reason }`, reason `hand_back`, `time_limit`, `idle`, `disconnect`, `taken_over`, `access_lost`, `agent_stopped` or `input_refused`), `AGENT_BROWSER_RESET` (`Agent browser reset`, one per browser reset), `AGENT_DISK_ALMOST_FULL` (`Disk almost full: 210 MB of 250 MB used.`, when the agent's files pass 80% of the plan's disk), `AGENT_DISK_FULL` (`Disk full: 260 MB of 250 MB used. The agent can't save new files until some are deleted.`), `AGENT_DISK_TEMP_CLEARED` (`Temporary files passed 1 GB, so the agent restarted and cleared them.`), `AGENT_DISK_HOST_RESTART` (`The agent restarted to clear its temporary files.`). Note rows with a `title` and no `ok`: `runtime_log_unavailable` (first row when the agent isn't running or its host doesn't answer; `Logs` and `LogsFile` then answer `result: true` for a day with who-did-what rows), `runtime_log_deleted` (first row of a day whose log was deleted on a later day). `token_usage` events add `{ model, tokens: { input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, total }, tokencost (cents), durationMs, calls }` (its `remainingcredits` is deprecated). AI usage is counted per LLM turn (one `token_usage` event per billed turn); Wiro model runs the agent starts are billed by Wiro from the wallet of the workspace that owns the agent's Wiro API key and carry no cost figure. A `cost` object (`{ credits, skill, action }`) can appear only on old events from before per-turn token billing. `tool` (only on `tool_*`): the name of the tool the agent used. A connector's tool is `<slug>__<tool>` (such as `wordpress__create_post`): `tool` and `title` are that name, `toolintegration` is the slug and `summary` is `{}`; a Reddit (`reddit`) call is titled `Reddit API operation`. `toolintegration` and `toolaction` (only on `tool_started` and `tool_completed`, only when a word fits, never both): the same closed-list words as timeline tool blocks (see Message/Detail); read them instead of parsing `title` or `summary`. `summary` is opaque structured payload (secret values such as apikey/apppassword/bearer/token are masked). `error`, on a failure row, is always `Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`; the failure's own reason never reaches the log. `userUuid: "system"` rows have `user: null`; rows without a `userUuid` resolve to the agent owner. Logs, LogsList, LogsFile and LogsDelete refuse an unknown or deleted agent with code 95 `User agent not found`, an outside caller with 96 `You don't have access to this user agent`, and a plain team member with 97 `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.`.
POST /UserAgent/LogsList: `{ useragentguid }` → `{ result, dates: [{ date, sizeBytes, compressed }] }` sorted newest-first. `sizeBytes` is 0 on a day with who-did-what rows and no log file. When the agent isn't running or its host doesn't answer and it has who-did-what days, the answer is still `result: true`, adds `runtimeUnavailable` (`not_running` or `no_answer`) and `note`, and `sizeBytes` is null.
POST /UserAgent/LogsFile: `{ useragentguid, date }` → `{ result, date, truncated, events }`. Full log of the day. Same event shape as /Logs, who-did-what rows and notes included.
POST /UserAgent/LogsDelete: `{ useragentguid, date }` → `{ result, date, removed: { plain, gz } }`. Removes the agent's own turns and tool calls for the day. Who-did-what rows stay, the date can stay in LogsList with `sizeBytes: 0`, and reads of an earlier day you deleted start with a `runtime_log_deleted` note.
POST /UserAgent/Realtime/ScreenInfo: `{ useragentguid }` → `{ result: true, errors: [], available, canControl, reason }`. Never refuses an agent; see the realtime endpoints above.
POST /UserAgent/Realtime/ScreenStart: `{ useragentguid, control? }` → `{ result, errors, wsUrl, screenToken, control, canControl, maxSeconds, idleSeconds? }`. A one-time ticket, valid 60 seconds, for the Screen socket; see the realtime endpoints above and Agent Chat Integration.
POST /UserAgent/RunStreamToken: `{ useragentguid }` → `{ result, runstreamtoken, expiresat, errors }`. `runstreamtoken` is an opaque token valid until `expiresat` (Unix seconds), 24 to 48 hours after it is issued; send it in `agent_run_subscribe` on the Agent WebSocket, keep it private, and get a new one when less than 12 hours remain. Same access as Logs: the owner (also with the owner's project API key) and, on a team agent, team admins; a stopped agent gets a token too. A failed call answers `result: false` with both set to null and one `errors` entry: code 0 `useragentguid is required`, 95 `User agent not found` (unknown or deleted agent), 96 `You don't have access to this user agent`, 97 `Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent.` (plain team member), or code 0 `runstream-unavailable` (following runs live is not available right now; try again later).
### Messaging

POST /UserAgent/Message/Send: `{ useragentguid, message, sessionkey?, callbackurl?, model? }` → `{ result, messageguid, agenttoken, status: "agent_queue", modelChangeMarker? }`. `model` (optional) overrides the agent's chat model for this turn only and must be a `selectable` slug from `tokenRates.models` (a model that a Model Access rule for the agent blocks, its own, the account's or team's, or the `agent` surface's, is refused with code 92); when it switches the session to a different chat model the response includes `modelChangeMarker: { guid, type: "model_change", fromModel, toModel, createdat }`, and a synthetic marker row (`status: "agent_done"`, `model: null`, `metadata.type: "model_change"`) is inserted into history. A reserved sessionkey (see DeleteSession) is refused with `Reserved sessionkey`, and more than 8 files with `Too many files (max 8)`. A reply Wiro handles itself as a setup reply (a yes that applies one setup card or gets Wiro's card listing, a yes while a sign-in or project connect card waits, a key pasted as the reply while the latest reply has one pending connect card and it is a key card with one secret field, another service's key pasted for that card, a refusal because the sender isn't an agent admin, or a no that turned cards down while the agent isn't running) runs no agent turn, costs nothing and is answered whatever the agent's status (a card applied while the agent is stopped doesn't start it; the change loads at its next start): `{ result: true, messageguid, agenttoken: null, status: "agent_end", content, response, setupresult: { applied: [ids], dismissed: [ids], failed: [{ id, error }], restarting, next? } }` (all lists empty for a card listing; `next` as under Setup From Chat); the stored row has `metadata.type: "setup_result"` and `model: null`, and Detail and History also return, in its `metadata`, `next` (as `setupresult.next`) and, for a card listing, `listed` (the card ids it showed) and `listedfrom` (the guid of the message they are on); a `callbackurl` gets the result right away with `status: "agent_end"`; `response` is English text, read `setupresult` in code. A slash command the agent doesn't run or has turned off in `enabledcommands` (such as `/status`) is answered by Wiro too, only while the agent's status is 4, with no turn and no charge, even while the agent is paused for its balance: `{ result: true, messageguid, agenttoken: null, status: "agent_end", content, response }` with no `setupresult`; `response` is "⛔ Unknown or disabled command: /<name>" (the name in lower case), with a second line "Send /agent_help to see the available commands." when the agent has agent_help on; it is stored and posted to `callbackurl` like a setup reply (`metadata.type: "setup_result"`, and the callback's `metadata` also has `cards: []` and `command`), and files sent with it are not kept. A command is a `/` at the start of the message or after whitespace, then a letter or `_`, anywhere in the text once links and lines starting with `>` are left out; a message holding one of the agent's enabled commands (in lower case, followed by whitespace or the end) goes to the agent; otherwise the first command decides, and `/model`, `/models`, `/start`, `/help`, `/settings`, `/app`, `/tmp`, `/run`, `/usr`, `/bin`, `/etc`, `/home`, `/var` and names over 32 characters go to the agent as usual (so do `/usr/bin/env` and `/start /pricing`). When Wiro removed a key from a message that still goes to the agent, the usual result adds `contentmasked: true` and `content` (the text the agent got, with `[key removed]`). While the agent's status isn't 4, every message Wiro doesn't answer itself as a setup reply (one with attachments or over 2,000 characters included) is refused with `agentstatus` (0 Stopped, 1 Stopping, 2 Queued, 3 Starting, 5 Error, 6 Setup Required); with status 1 the error reads "Agent is stopping. Please wait a moment and try again." when the agent is shutting down to stay stopped and "Agent is restarting. Please wait a moment and try again." when it is shutting down to start again, as in a restart. A used-up spend limit that covers the agent (its own; once the plan's included AI usage is used up, also the account's or team's and the `agent` surface's) answers code 93 with `agentstatus` (4) and a message that names the limit and when it resets, or code 0 `Spend limits could not be checked. Try again in a moment.` when the limits can't be checked; nothing is queued or charged. After that check, when the plan's included AI usage is used up and the balance is under $0.50, Send answers code 97 with `agentstatus` and `agentusage` (`pausedreason: "balance"`; see Pricing Model), and a running agent with no active plan gets code 97 with the same fields (`agentusage.pausedreason: "plan"`) and `<Agent name> has no active plan. Choose a plan to keep it running.` (renew the plan with RenewSubscription; adding funds doesn't run it). A deleted agent answers code 95, `User agent not found`.
POST /UserAgent/Message/Detail: `{ messageguid }` or `{ agenttoken }` (optional `sessionkey` scopes the read to one session) → `{ result, data: { guid, uuid, agenttoken, user, sessionkey, content, response, debugoutput, timeline, status, metadata, attachments, deletestatus, createdat, startedat, endedat, inputtokens, outputtokens, cachereadtokens, cachewritetokens, totaltokens, model, tokencost, processedms } }`. `timeline[]` is the authoritative ordered turn record. The complete public block shape is `{ blockid, callindex, contentindex, type: "reasoning"|"answer"|"tool"|"setup", text, phase: "stream"|"end"|"error", version, startedat, updatedat }`, setup blocks also carry `setup` (see Setup From Chat), and tool blocks also carry `{ toollabel, toolstatus: "requested"|"completed"|"error", toolintegration, toolaction }` (reasoning and answer blocks have none of these four keys); no additional internal correlation or execution fields are returned in timeline blocks. Reasoning text is a model-provided reasoning summary, never raw chain-of-thought; tool blocks expose only `toollabel`, `toolstatus`, `toolintegration`, and `toolaction`. `toolintegration` is the connector the step works in, as its `slug` from POST /AgentConnector/List (such as "shopify", "google-ads", "serper" or "wiro"; channels such as Telegram get no word), or null; a step that calls a connector's tool has that tool's name as its `toollabel`, `<slug>__<tool>` (such as `shopify__list_products`). `toolaction` is what the step does, or null: "screenshot"|"open-page"|"read-page"|"click"|"type"|"press-key"|"wait"|"upload"|"download"|"read-file"|"edit-media". A block never has both; both are null when no word fits and on blocks saved before these fields existed; the words come with the block's first `requested` update and every later update carries them; a later update can carry a different word if the step changed, so read them from the newest version; a block whose step is rewritten and no longer fits a word keeps its last word; treat a value you don't know like null. Merge by `blockid`, accept only a strictly newer per-block `version`, then sort by `callindex`, `contentindex`, and `blockid`. When a turn ends with `agent_error` or `agent_cancel`, the server closes every block still at `stream` and sends each one as an `agent_timeline_delta`, usually just before that final event. After `agent_end`, open blocks normally close a few seconds later. A tool block that closed with `toolstatus` `requested` was cut off before it finished. Assistant rows also carry token columns + `model` + `tokencost` + `processedms`.
POST /UserAgent/Message/History: `{ useragentguid, sessionkey?, limit?, before? }` → `{ result, data: { messages, count, hasmore, sessiontoken? } }`. Each message row carries the fields of Message/Detail except `sessionkey`, `startedat` and `endedat`, including persisted `timeline[]`, `uuid`, `agenttoken`, decorated `user`, and token columns. Per-turn model switches surface as synthetic `model_change` marker rows (`status: "agent_done"`, `metadata.type: "model_change"`). Collaborative team mode returns rows from all team members, and the agent keeps one shared memory for the team; private mode filters by caller uuid and keeps per-operator memory. `sessiontoken` follows the session live on the Agent WebSocket (`agent_session_subscribe`). A reserved sessionkey (see DeleteSession) returns an empty page (`messages: []`). Messages the agent adds between turns (a scheduled report, files sent after an answer, the result of background work) are finished rows (`status: "agent_end"`, empty `content`; `metadata.type` is `"subagent"` for the result of background work, `"system"` otherwise) with no `agenttoken` stream and no `callbackurl` call; a turn that moves work to the background ends with a short line saying the result will follow.
POST /UserAgent/Message/Sessions: `{ useragentguid }` → `{ result, data: { sessions: [{ sessionkey, messagecount, updatedat, lastmessage, name? }] } }`. `name` is the optional display-name overlay (set via RenameSession); `model_change` marker rows are excluded from session counts / lastmessage; named-but-empty sessions surface with messagecount 0.
POST /UserAgent/Message/RenameSession: `{ useragentguid, sessionkey, name }` → `{ result, errors }`. Sets a display `name` (sanitized, ≤40 chars) on the session (stored separately from the messages); the `sessionkey` and the agent's memory are unchanged. Calling it with a brand-new sessionkey before any Send creates a named-but-empty session that immediately lists. Reserved system keys reject with `"Session not found"`.
POST /UserAgent/Message/DeleteSession: `{ useragentguid, sessionkey, rotate? }`. Hard delete (permanent, not hidden). `rotate: true` (default false) also clears the agent's memory of this session; the `name` overlay is dropped. The call only purges the caller's own messages. Even in a collaborative team session, you can't wipe another participant's history. Passing a reserved sessionkey (`wiro:api` or one that starts with `wiro:api:`, one that starts with `voice-prep`, `voice-call-`, `cs-cron-` or `cron:`, or one that contains `:cron:`) returns `"Session not found"` instead of a delete.
POST /UserAgent/Message/Delete: `{ useragentguid, items: [{ messageguid, side: "user"|"agent"|"both" }] }`. Per-side soft-delete via the `deletestatus` bitmask: user → 1, agent → 3, both → 3 (agent collapses to 3 because total-disappearance is the user-facing intent). `Message/History` only returns messages whose `deletestatus` is 0 (any bit set hides the message). Only messages whose `uuid` is the caller's are affected; any other `messageguid` is skipped silently. On a team agent, any active member of the agent's team can call it from the team's workspace; it still hides only their own messages. Best-effort across the items array.
POST /UserAgent/Message/Cancel: `{ messageguid }` or `{ agenttoken }` (optional `sessionkey` scopes the cancel to one session). Only cancellable in agent_queue/agent_start/agent_output.
POST /UserAgent/Message/SetupCardApply: `{ useragentguid, messageguid, cardid, action: "apply"|"dismiss", values?, signin?, redirecturl?, wiroprojectguid? }` → `{ result, errors, setup, restarting, summary, authorizeUrl?, paired?, errorcode?, next? }`. Applies or dismisses one pending setup card (the stored card, checked again against the agent's current setup; never applied twice). Apply needs an agent admin (owner or team admin); any member who can see the chat can dismiss; the message must be one the caller can read with Message/History. A connect card connects through ConnectorConnect's own checks: a `key` card takes `values` for its `fields` (the connector's Connect fields as AgentConnector/Detail `credentialfields` name them; checked for required, format, pattern and maxlength, a json field also takes an object; a refused value saves nothing and keeps the card pending); a `project` card, for Wiro AI Models (`wiro`), takes `wiroprojectguid` and no `values`, and that project becomes the agent's own Wiro project as with CredentialProjectBind (left out with a project API key: that key's own project; a card that can't connect without one stays pending with `Pick a project on the card to connect <Title>.`). A `signin` card answers `{ result: true, authorizeUrl, setup: <still pending>, next }`: `values` carries the fields its sign-in takes (your own app's keys for a connector that signs in with one; a card from a project-API-key turn never signs in with Wiro's app), `redirecturl` is where the browser returns (Wiro's own return page when left out, so send your own); once the browser is back with `connector_connected=true`, apply the card again to record it applied (or it is recorded the next time a card of the same person's is applied or dismissed in that chat). On an add card, `values` are its one pending key card's values and `signin: true` finishes its one pending sign-in card once the connector reads connected: both cards apply in one step with one restart, `summary` names both ("Google Play Promotional Content added. Google Play Console connected."), and `paired: [{ setup, result, error }]` is the connect card after the call; a `project` card always takes its own step. Refusals: `This card takes no key. Apply it without one.`, `This card brings more than one key. Apply it, then add each key on its own card.`, `This card has no sign-in to finish. Apply it without one.` (errorcode signin_no_pair), `This card brings more than one sign-in. Apply it, then connect each on its own card.` (signin_many), `<Title> is not connected yet. Finish the sign-in on the card first.` (not_connected), `Send values or signin, not both.`, `redirecturl must be a URL.`, `wiroprojectguid must be a project's id.`, and ConnectorConnect's own sentences (a field's, such as `Client ID is required. Client Secret is required.` for a sign-in sent without your app's keys, the vendor's, `Invalid redirect URL`). `setup` is the card after the action, or null when the call is refused before the card is read; `summary` is a short English phrase. `Setup from chat is off for this agent.` when chatsetup is "off", or the call is sent with a project API key and chatsetup is "webchat". A skill update, append or revert card whose skill text no longer matches its `before` fails with `This skill changed after the card was made. Ask the agent again.`; an add or remove card whose change no longer matches the agent's skills fails with `This agent's connectors or skills changed after the card was made. Ask the agent again.`; a connect card whose connector left the catalog fails with `<Title> can't be connected any more.`. `next` (only when the call leaves something to connect): `[{ connector, title, mode: "key"|"signin"|"project", cardid?, messageguid? }]`, for a Connect button in your own product. Full flow: https://wiro.ai/docs/agent-chat-integration

Setup From Chat: an agent never changes its own setup and never sees a key; it proposes a setup card that Wiro checks and stores on the operator's message, shown as a `setup` timeline block (`text: null`, sorted after the turn's other blocks, `phase: "end"`, at most three per message; a pending connect card's block also has `next: [{ connector, title, mode }]`, its own connector, gone once the card is acted on). `setup` = `{ v: 1, id (12 lower-case letters and digits), kind: "add"|"remove"|"connect"|"disconnect"|"schedule"|"skill"|"timezone", action? (schedule: create|update|pause|resume|delete; skill: create|update|append|revert|disable|enable), connector? (connect and disconnect: the connector's catalog slug, such as serper or hubspot; never a channel, a credential or a value), title? (connect and disconnect: the connector's title, written by Wiro), authtype?, mode? ("key"|"signin"|"project") and fields? (connect only, written by Wiro: the card's form in the shape of AgentConnector/Detail credentialfields; a signin card's fields are the fields its sign-in takes, such as your own app's serveronly keys; a project card's one field has `source: "wiro_project"`, a project picker), wiroapp? (connect, only on a card from a Wiro web chat turn), key? (add and remove: one skill util-<name> as Skills/List names it, ≤64; schedule and skill: cs-cron-<name> or cs-<name>), title? (schedule and skill: ≤80), cron? (5 fields, agent time zone, at most hourly from chat), instructions? (create/update: the full text, ≤20000; append: only the text to add; revert: the text it restores, written by Wiro), before? (skill update/append/revert only, written by Wiro), with? (add and remove, written by Wiro: the other skills turned on or off with key, ≤12), pauses? and resumes? (add and remove, written by Wiro: scheduled tasks that pause or run again, ≤20 each), needs? (add only, written by Wiro: the connectors the change works with that aren't connected yet, ≤3, each { connector, title, mode: "key"|"signin"|"project" }, each with its own connect card on the same message while there is room), timezone? (IANA), note? (≤300), status?: "pending"|"applied"|"dismissed"|"failed" (absent = pending), actedat?, actedby?, error? (failed only), requestedby, createdat }`; skip a card whose kind or action you don't know. An `add` card turns on one skill and a `remove` card turns one off, at no charge, and the agent restarts; connectors are not added or removed: a connected connector is on. A `connect` card names an active catalog connector the agent doesn't have connected (a channel is refused with `Telegram is a channel: it is connected in the agent's settings.`): mode `key` takes the connector's fields (SetupCardApply `values`, or the key pasted as the reply when the card has one secret field), mode `signin` (oauth and provider-oauth connectors) gets `authorizeUrl` from SetupCardApply and is recorded applied once the connector reads connected; a typed reply never starts a sign-in; mode `project`, for Wiro AI Models (`wiro`), takes one of your projects as SetupCardApply `wiroprojectguid`, never from a typed reply. Account pickers are chosen after connecting, with ConnectorSetAccounts (https://wiro.ai/docs/agent-connectors). A `disconnect` card disconnects a connector the agent has a connection for, as ConnectorDisconnect does; channels are changed outside the chat, and a disconnect card for Wiro AI Models (`wiro`) leaves the agent's Wiro project in place. A skill `append` card adds text to the end of an existing skill; a `revert` card undoes the skill's last change; show `before` next to the text after the change. An agent admin approves one card at a time: by replying with only an approval word (yes, ok, approve, go ahead, evet, 👍, ...) via Message/Send in the same session, by pressing Apply on the card in the Wiro web chat, or with Message/SetupCardApply. A typed yes acts only on pending cards of the agent's latest reply that are less than 30 minutes old and applies only a card whose exact content Wiro has shown: on a message sent with a project API key, the first yes gets the card listing ("Card 1: Add <Title> (skill).", the text a card carries quoted with "> ", a disconnect card as "Card N: Disconnect <Connector> (what was saved to connect it is removed)."; connect cards that take values, sign in or pick a project are not listed) and a second yes applies it; with several cards, "yes N" applies card N. no/cancel dismisses the pending cards; a yes never applies a connect card that takes values, and a yes while a signin card waits is answered `A yes cannot connect <Title>. Its sign-in and any app keys are entered outside this chat, never in it.` (a project card: `A yes cannot connect <Title>. Its project is picked outside this chat.`) with nothing applied. Wiro's answer lines include "✅ Applied: <summary>.", "⚠️ Not applied: <reason>", "Your agent is restarting to load the change. Continue in about a minute.", "Next: paste your <Title> key as your reply.", "Next: connect <Title> to finish. Its sign-in and any app keys are entered outside this chat, never in it.", "Next: connect <Title> to finish. Its project is picked outside this chat.", "⚠️ Not saved: <reason>. Paste the key again as your reply.", "That does not look like a <Title> key (it looks like <kind>), so it was not saved. Paste the <Title> key as your reply.", "Only an agent admin can apply setup changes." and "The setup change was turned down.". Keys: when the latest reply has one pending connect card and it is a key card with one secret field, an agent admin can paste the key as the reply; Wiro saves it to the connector, marks the card applied and stores `[key saved to <Connector title>]` instead; in other messages Wiro replaces clear keys with `[key removed]`. From a backend, connect connectors with ConnectorConnect and save channel keys with CredentialUpsert rather than in a message. The agent's `chatsetup` setting decides where cards work: "all" (default: Wiro web chat and messages sent with a project API key), "webchat" (Wiro web chat only), "off" (never). A message sent with a project API key acts with the key owner's rights even when an end user typed it, so agents your customers talk to should use "webchat" or "off". Telegram, Slack and Discord messages never get or approve a card. Studio and the Workflow Agent always have setup from chat off. To show all of this in your own product, with every request and answer, follow https://wiro.ai/docs/agent-chat-integration.

Message statuses: agent_queue → agent_start → agent_output (multiple) → agent_end. Also: agent_error, agent_cancel. `agent_done` is used only on synthetic `model_change` marker rows. Failed turns: on agent_error / agent_cancel, `response` and `debugoutput` (and the WebSocket event `message` and the webhook) hold one message, a code in brackets and a fixed sentence, never the underlying error: `[SECURITY_BLOCKED] The agent's security rules blocked this message. Change it and send it again.`; `[SAFETY_POLICY_BLOCKED] The model's provider declined this request under its safety policy. Rephrase it and send it again.`; `[TURN_INTERRUPTED] This request was interrupted by a restart before it finished. Please send it again.`; `[SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED] This agent's spend limit is used up, so it paused. It runs again when the limit resets or is raised.` (a spend limit that covers the agent: its own, or once its included usage is used up the account's, team's or `agent` surface's); `[USAGE_CEILING_REACHED] This agent reached its hourly or daily safety ceiling for AI model calls, so it paused. It runs again when that hour or day is over.`, `[MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED] This agent's Model Access rule blocks the model it uses, so it stopped. It runs again once the model is allowed or another one is chosen.`; `[CREDITS_EXHAUSTED] This agent's plan usage and its owner's balance are used up, so it paused. It runs again once its owner adds funds or its plan renews.` (the plan's included AI usage and the balance are used up; a turn already running stops at its next model call, and every try fails until funds are added or the plan renews); `[AGENT_UNAVAILABLE] Agent is temporarily unavailable. Please try again shortly.`; `[REQUEST_CANCELLED] Request cancelled.`. [SECURITY_BLOCKED]: the agent's security rules blocked the message (it can also come with agent_end, when the block came back as the answer, so match the codes on `response` whatever the status); [SAFETY_POLICY_BLOCKED]: the model's provider declined it under its safety policy; [TURN_INTERRUPTED]: the agent restarted mid-turn; [CREDITS_EXHAUSTED]: the included AI usage and the balance are used up, add funds or wait for the plan to renew; [AGENT_UNAVAILABLE]: any other failure; [REQUEST_CANCELLED]: cancelled (agent_cancel). Match the code, not the sentence.

### Agent WebSocket

Same server: wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1. Subscribe per-turn: `{ "type": "agent_info", "agenttoken": "..." }` with the agenttoken from Message/Send (30 letters and digits). Missing → `{ "type": "error", "message": "agenttoken-required", "result": false }`; a value that is not 30 letters and digits (a session key, for example) → `{ "type": "error", "message": "agenttoken-invalid", "result": false }` and no subscription. Up to 256 agenttokens per connection; one more drops the oldest.

Events: agent_subscribed (status + provisional debugoutput + persisted timeline[]), agent_start, agent_timeline_delta (`{ messageguid, block }`, one public block update), agent_output (provisional cumulative SSE answer: raw, answer, speed, tokenCount, wordCount), agent_end (final answer), agent_usage_report (arrives after agent_end on the same channel: `{ messageguid, model, inputtokens, outputtokens, cachereadtokens, cachewritetokens, totaltokens, tokencost (cents) }`; its `remainingcredits` is deprecated), agent_error (a string: the coded failure message, see Failed turns), agent_cancel (`[REQUEST_CANCELLED] Request cancelled.`). agent_wiroai_runtask (fires when the agent itself launches a Wiro model run mid-turn, e.g. image/video for a skill or through the Wiro AI Models connector, `wiro`; arrives on the turn's agenttoken with `{ taskid, socketaccesstoken, slugowner, slugproject, categories, status }`; subscribe to its socketaccesstoken via `task_info` to stream task_queue→task_postprocess_end and collect media outputs; NOT emitted for /Run calls you make yourself; it fires only for model runs the agent starts while answering your Message/Send turn).

Follow a session: send `{ "type": "agent_session_subscribe", "sessiontoken": "<from Message/History>" }` → `{ "type": "agent_session_subscribed", "result": true }`. Each message added to the session between turns then arrives as `agent_message_inserted` `{ sessiontoken, message: { guid, uuid, sessionkey, content, response, status: "agent_end", metadata, createdat, startedat, endedat }, result: true }`. `agent_session_unsubscribe` stops (no reply). Up to 16 sessions per connection; following another drops the oldest follow. Malformed token → `{ "type": "error", "message": "sessiontoken-invalid", "result": false }`. Frames are not replayed: subscribe again after a reconnect and read History once.

Follow an agent's background runs (its Scheduled Tasks, background work and other runs with no chat message, plus every Wiro model run it starts, chat turns included; labels only, never reasoning or answer text): send `{ "type": "agent_run_subscribe", "useragentguid": "<guid>", "runstreamtoken": "<from POST /UserAgent/RunStreamToken>" }` → `{ type: "agent_run_subscribed", useragentguid, expiresat, runs, models, dropped, result: true }`. `expiresat` is the token's. `runs` (open runs, most recently active first, up to 256): `{ runref, runkind, sessionkey, root, startedat, steps, block }`; `models` (open model runs, newest `startedat` first, up to 256): `{ modelref, runref, sessionkey, slugowner, slugproject, categories, startedat }`; `dropped`: guids this connection stopped following to make room. Events can arrive just before the reply. Subscribing again is fine: fresh lists, and the subscription ends at the sent token's `expiresat`. `{ "type": "agent_run_unsubscribe", "useragentguid": "<guid>" }` → `{ type: "agent_run_unsubscribed", useragentguid, result: true }` (no token; also for an agent you weren't following; a malformed guid gets no reply).

Run events are `{ type, useragentguid, message, result: true }` (no agenttoken or other token; `result` stays true when a run fails, so read `ok`). `agent_run_start` `{ runref, runkind, sessionkey, root, startedat }`, `agent_run_block` `{ runref, runkind, sessionkey, root, block }` (only a newer block version) and `agent_run_end` `{ runref, runkind, sessionkey, root, ok, reason, durationms, endedat }` (once; nothing after it) cover runs with no chat message; `agent_run_model_start` `{ modelref, runref, sessionkey, slugowner, slugproject, categories, startedat }` and `agent_run_model_end` `{ modelref, ok, outcome, durationms, endedat }` cover every model run the agent starts, chat turns included. A model run, or rarely a block, can come before its run's start: treat the run as open. Fields: `runref` and `modelref` are 22 characters of `[A-Za-z0-9_-]`; `runref` is null only on model events and `models` items a chat turn started; `modelref` is not a taskid (this stream has no taskid or socketaccesstoken). `runkind`: `cron` (Scheduled Task) | `subagent` | `announce` (writes the result of background work back to its chat) | `other`; it can change from `other` to a specific kind, never back, and the value on `agent_run_end` is final. `root`: `chat` | `cron` | `unknown` (never back to `unknown`), not on model events. `sessionkey`: the chat session's key as `Message/Send` and `Message/Sessions` use it, not its display name (up to 512 characters of ASCII letters, digits and `._:~@+-`, else null; a Scheduled Task has null or its `cs-cron-` key) or null, never back to null once set; on model events, the key sent with the request that started the model run. Whoever starts a session or a model run picks its key: escape it before display and don't rely on it to tell who started a run. `startedat`, `endedat` and `expiresat` are integer Unix seconds; `durationms` is integer milliseconds, never null. `ok`: true | false | null (null only with `reason` or `outcome` `lost`). `reason`: `report` | `terminal` (after the run's last update to a running step, a step ended or failed and no step was running again within two minutes; the first step to end or fail after that update sets `ok` and `endedat`) | `lost` (60 minutes of silence, still open 48 hours after it started, or the agent stopped, restarted or was deleted; `endedat` is the last activity). `outcome`: `done` (`task_postprocess_end` with `pexit` "0") | `failed` (`task_error`, or another `pexit`) | `cancelled` (`task_cancel`) | `lost` (for example still open after 24 hours). `slugowner` and `slugproject`: up to 128 of `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` or null. `categories`: up to 16 strings, never null. `steps` (in `runs`): tool steps so far. `block`: an `agent_timeline_delta` block with `text: null` (null in `runs` until the run has one); key by `runref` + `blockid` and keep only a higher `version`; `phase` `stream` | `end` | `error` (end and error stay); `toolstatus` `requested` | `completed` | `error`; `toolintegration` and `toolaction` from the timeline closed lists, never both; an update with no tool word keeps the last word.

Run stream errors keep the connection open: `{ "type": "error", "message": "runstreamtoken-invalid", "useragentguid": "<guid>" or null, "result": false }` (wrong, another agent's or expired token, or a malformed guid or token; the guid is null when malformed) → get a new token at most once a minute and subscribe again; `{ "type": "error", "message": "runstream-unavailable", "useragentguid": "<guid>", "result": false }` (the lists could not be read, or the stream is not available; never sent as empty lists) → keep what you hold and retry later. Limits: 256 agents per connection (one more drops the oldest subscription, listed in `dropped`; expired ones are removed first and not listed), 256 items each in `runs` and `models` (an agent can have more than 256 open model runs: `models` then holds the 256 newest), 256 open runs per agent (a run that starts while 256 are open is sent late: at its next step once one has ended, or with its end), 16 categories, a 512-character sessionkey, 512 blocks per run (later new blocks are not sent; the end still comes); a subscription ends at its `expiresat`. Client rules: key runs by `runref`, blocks by `runref` + `blockid`, model runs by `modelref`; on `agent_run_subscribed` replace the open runs and model runs with the lists, except ones first seen after you sent that subscribe and, when `models` has 256 items, the model runs it leaves out; a run missing from a list has ended (result unknown), and so has a model run missing from a `models` list of fewer than 256 items; keep ended refs for at least 10 minutes and never reopen them; `agent_run_block` or `agent_run_model_start` for an unknown ref opens it; when `agent_run_block`, `agent_run_end` or `agent_run_model_end` for an agent you follow names a run or model run you don't hold, send `agent_run_subscribe` again for that agent, at most once every 30 seconds, so its reply brings what you hold up to date (one already waiting for its reply is enough); after a reconnect, subscribe again for every agent; while something is open, subscribe again after 30 seconds with no `agent_run_*` frame; with no reply within 10 seconds, resend after 5, 15, then 60 seconds; renew when less than 12 hours remain.

One turn can be Thinking → Answer/Tool → Thinking → Answer. Merge each `agent_timeline_delta.message.block` by `blockid` and strictly newer per-block `version`; do not compare versions across blocks or append in arrival order. Sort by `callindex`, `contentindex`, and `blockid`. `agent_output` remains provisional cumulative SSE output until the corresponding answer block catches up; Message/Detail is authoritative. A `setup` block (a setup change the agent proposes) arrives as `agent_timeline_delta` too; read its later `status` from Message/Detail or Message/History.

`result: true` for success events (every `agent_run_*` frame too, even an end with `ok: false`), `false` for error/cancel (including `runstreamtoken-invalid` and `runstream-unavailable`). Output contains full accumulated text (replace, don't append).

The agent's live Screen is not on this socket: it has its own, wss://socket.wiro.ai/v1/AgentRealtime/Screen, opened with a one-time screenToken from POST /UserAgent/Realtime/ScreenStart (see the realtime endpoints above).

### Agent Webhooks

Include `callbackurl` in Message/Send (a public http(s) address; a host that is or resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address gets no webhook). Wiro POSTs when agent finishes (a setup reply Wiro handles itself, or an unknown or disabled slash command, runs no turn and posts right away with `status: "agent_end"`; its `metadata` is `{ type: "setup_result", via, cards, next?, listed?, listedfrom?, teamguid? }`, or for a command `{ type: "setup_result", via, cards: [], command, teamguid? }`; `via` is `"api"` for a project API key, `"web"` otherwise):
`{ messageguid, status, content, response, debugoutput, metadata: { raw, answer, speed, wordCount, ... }, endedat }`
For cancel, and for an error that cut the turn off (such as `[TURN_INTERRUPTED]`): `metadata` is `{}`; a turn that ended with a coded failure (such as `[SPEND_LIMIT_REACHED]`) posts the usual progressGenerate metadata with the coded text in `raw` and `answer`, so read the outcome from `status` and `response`. Retry: 3 tries in all, 2s apart; any 2xx answer counts as delivered, and any other answer (a 3xx redirect included) or no answer is tried again.
Webhooks do not embed timeline blocks; fetch Message/Detail by `messageguid` for authoritative `timeline[]`.

### Connectors

A connector gives an agent the tools of one outside service; each is a catalog row named by its `slug` (`serper`, `shopify`, `facebook-pages`, `google-ads`, ...), with a public page at https://wiro.ai/connectors/{slug}. Always the customer's own credentials. Full cycle with every request and answer: https://wiro.ai/docs/agent-connectors

Catalog (public, no auth): POST /AgentConnector/List `{ search?, category? }` (category: ads, ai, analytics, commerce, content, crm, data, email, marketing, messaging, productivity, social or stores) and POST /AgentConnector/Detail `{ slug }` → `agentconnectors: [{ slug, title, description, category, iconurl, websiteurl, authtype: "fields"|"provider-oauth"|"headers"|"oauth"|"none", transport: "local"|"streamable-http"|"sse", credentialfields: [{ name, label, description (Markdown), required, secret, format: text|password|url|email|textarea|json|select, options?, placeholder?, pattern?, maxlength?, serveronly?, mode?: "oauth"|"key" (oauth: a field of the sign-in way, your app's keys or another value it needs), source? }], accountpickers: [{ key, label, description, multiple }], scopes, modes: ["oauth"]|["oauth","key"]|[], wiroapp, tools: [{ name, title, description, readonly, destructive }] (a connector on a vendor's own MCP server, tiktok-ads, dataforseo, lemlist, gitbook, hackmd or wiro, lists none until an agent first connects it), docs: { overview, setup, revoke, limits } | null, sortorder, updatedat }]`. Never a value.

Connect: POST /UserAgent/ConnectorConnect `{ useragentguid, slug, values?, mode?, redirecturl?, accounts?, wiroprojectguid? }` (owner or team admin). `fields` and `headers` rows: `values` `{ <field name>: value }`, never for a `source: "wiro_project"` field (Wiro AI Models takes `wiroprojectguid` instead) (a field left out keeps its saved value, "" or null clears it; formats, `pattern` and `maxlength` checked; where the row has a credential check, one read call to the vendor first, and a refusal answers `result: false` with the vendor's own sentence and saves nothing) → `{ status: "connected", applied: 1|0, restart: "scheduled"|"none"|"failed", useragentconnectors: [<connection>] }`. Field values are at most 65,536 characters (a `json` field also takes an object); a `headers` row's values at most 4,096 characters on one line, named by their `name` in refusals (lemlist `apikey`, DataForSEO `login` and `password`, GitBook and HackMD `token`; labels made from the names, a secret with `format: "password"`). `provider-oauth` rows (vendors that sign in with an app the customer owns): `mode: "oauth"` (default) with the app's client id and secret (`serveronly` fields) in `values` plus the other fields the sign-in needs (no `mode` or `mode: "oauth"`: Shopify `shopdomain`, LinkedIn `organizationid`, Reddit `developerprofileusername`), or `mode: "key"` for a key or token way in (Meta System User token, Mailchimp API key, Shopify client credentials) → connected with `authmode: "key"`. `oauth` rows (a vendor's own MCP server with its own sign-in, such as tiktok-ads): `redirecturl` only. Sign-ins (`provider-oauth` mode oauth, `oauth` rows) → `{ status: "pending", authorizeUrl }`: open it in the browser (10 minutes, once); the vendor redirects to https://api.wiro.ai/v1/AgentConnector/OAuthCallback (register it as the redirect URI of your own app), Wiro stores the tokens, restarts the agent and 302s to `redirecturl` + `connector_connected=true` or `connector_error=<code>` (authorization_denied, session_expired, token_exchange_failed, oauth_app_missing, oauth_app_changed, invalid_signature, invalid_shop, invalid_state, connector_unavailable, useragent_not_found, internal_error). `redirecturl`: https on any host, or http on localhost/127.0.0.1; without it the browser returns to wiro.ai's own connect-return page; the return carries no slug, so put what you need in `redirecturl`. With a project API key the vendor's consent screen names the integrator (organization, else team, else account) or the integrator's own app; `wiroapp` rows sign in with Wiro's app only from Wiro's own panel. The redirect URI (on the API host) can still show on some vendors' consent screens, and the own-app fields' help text names it. Wiro AI Models (`wiro`, Wiro's own model and task tools as `wiro__<tool>`: search_models, explore, recommend_model, get_model_schema, get_task_price, run_model, get_task, wait_for_task, list_tasks, cancel_task, kill_task, upload_file and the read-only search_docs and get_playbook, never more, and never a tool whose name has agent, workflow, billing, account, project, studio, credential, oauth, skill, spend, limit, access, wallet, team, organization, coupon, invoice, payment, key or user in it; they always act with the agent's own Wiro project key, so they are the agent's own calls: its spend limit and Model Access rule apply, and account, agent, team and billing endpoints are refused; wiroapiallowedpaths doesn't cover them; list_tasks, get_task, wait_for_task, get_task_price, cancel_task and kill_task work only on the tasks the agent started, with the connector or from the agent's skills: a task anyone else started, such as another agent on the same project, a person on wiro.ai or your own backend, is not listed, and the other tools answer for it as for a task that does not exist, while your own backend, calling with an API key of the agent's workspace, still sees every task in it; on an agent several of your users share, each of them can reach the runs the agent made for the others, so use one agent per customer to keep them apart): `wiroprojectguid` = a project id from Project/List, which becomes the agent's own Wiro project exactly as CredentialProjectBind binds it (a project API key may leave it out to bind its own project; without either, the agent's own project in its workspace is kept); ConnectorList shows the agent's current project as `wiroprojectid` (a string; null when the agent has none, and then it gets no wiro tools); moving the agent to a workspace its project isn't in disconnects the project and deletes the Wiro AI Models connection (CONNECTOR_DISCONNECTED, `summary.reason: "workspace"`), and so does deleting the team that owns the project, or that team's organization, for an agent of another workspace that runs with it, which then restarts (only a personal agent of the project's creator keeps it). `wiroprojectguid` on a connector whose tools run inside the agent is refused with `This connector takes no Wiro project.`; a vendor MCP connector without a project field ignores it.

State: POST /UserAgent/ConnectorList `{ useragentguid }` → `useragentconnectors[]` with `status` connected | pending (sign-in started, or the connection misses a required value) | reauth (sign-in expired or revoked, or `lasterror: "auth_changed"` when the connection holds a way in the connector no longer takes, a Gmail app password or a sign-in with Wiro's own app on a connector whose `wiroapp` is false: sign in again with an OAuth app of your own; the tools answer that it must be connected again until the next restart, then are gone) | error (`lasterror` code), `authmode` own|key|wiro for provider-oauth, `catalogstatus` active|hidden|retired, `savedvariables` (names only), `accounts`, token expiries (Wiro refreshes the access token itself, except on a Facebook Pages or Meta Ads sign-in: Meta's token lasts about 60 days and cannot be refreshed, so when it runs out the connector's next use or an account listing sets the connection to `reauth` with `lasterror: "token_not_refreshable"` and the customer signs in again; a System User token, `mode: "key"`, set never to expire avoids this), `scope` (sign-ins: the scopes the vendor granted, as it sent them; when the token answer names none, as Facebook's, the scopes Wiro asked for, separated by spaces, such as `mcp:tt4b` for tiktok-ads).

Accounts (a local connector lists candidates with a read tool of its own; a vendor MCP connector with pickers, such as tiktok-ads `advertisers`, with a read tool of the vendor's server and the connection's sign-in; with no pickers, ConnectorAccounts answers `pickers: []` for a local connector and `This connector has no accounts to pick.` for a vendor MCP connector, and ConnectorSetAccounts answers `This connector has no accounts to pick.` for either): POST /UserAgent/ConnectorAccounts `{ useragentguid, slug }` → `pickers: [{ key, label, description, multiple, candidates: [{ id, name }], selected }]` listed live from the vendor; POST /UserAgent/ConnectorSetAccounts `{ useragentguid, slug, accounts: { <key>: [ids] } }` → `{ accounts, applied, restart, useragentconnectors }`, every id checked against a fresh list, a single picker takes one, a picker left out keeps its selection. Tools refuse any account outside the selection.
