A sign-in that could not be refreshed, or that the vendor's server refuses (HTTP 401 or 403) as Wiro lists the accounts, sets the connection to `reauth` (a refused one with `lasterror` `unauthorized`, or `no_access_token` when it holds no token); that, and any list or save of a connection already `reauth`, answers `The sign-in for this connector expired or was revoked, so it has to be connected again. Ask the agent's operator to reconnect it.` with the error `code` `"reauth"` (the other refusals carry 0): sign in again. A refresh that failed for now, with the token already expired, answers `The token could not be refreshed right now. Try again in a moment.`; a vendor that refuses to list the accounts answers with its own sentence (a saved value or token in it reads `[redacted]`; with no sentence, `The connector could not complete the request.`). TikTok Ads: sign in with `redirecturl`, ConnectorAccounts lists `advertisers` as `{ id, name }`, and ConnectorSetAccounts `{ accounts: { advertisers: [ids] } }` saves the ones the agent may use. Campaigns, ad groups, campaign copies, and Smart+ campaigns, ad groups and ads the agent creates start paused; a call naming a Business Center (`bc_id`) is refused before it leaves the agent; Business Center, billing and payment, TikTok One, Creator Marketplace and Reach & Frequency buying tools are not offered.

Disconnect: POST /UserAgent/ConnectorDisconnect `{ useragentguid, slug }` → `{ removed, revoked, restart }`. Disconnecting Wiro AI Models (`wiro`) removes only the connection: the agent keeps its Wiro project, and the models its Skills run keep using it; only its `wiro__*` tools go after the restart.

The agent: after the restart, every connected connection of an active connector gives the agent its tools, named `<slug>__<tool>` (`serper__web_search`); name them in a Custom Skill to tell the agent when to use them. Access codes: 95 not found, 96 no access, 97 team admin required.

Connectors, Skills and Credentials: a connected connector is on; it is never a Skill to turn on or a credential to save. Deploy `skills` and SkillsApply take util-* Skills only. Deploy refuses a connector's slug in `credentials` (`Unknown credential: <key>. Connect a connector after the deploy with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect.`) and a `skills` name that isn't a Skill (`Unknown skill: <name>.`; a name that starts with int-: `Unknown skill: <name>. Connectors are connected with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect, not turned on as skills.`), before anything is created or charged; SkillsApply answers `Unknown skill: <name>`; a CredentialUpsert row whose `credentialkey` is a connector's slug refuses the whole request (`Unknown credential: <key>. Connectors are connected with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect.`); Credentials/Detail answers `Credential not found: <key>` (code 404) for a connector's slug. The Twilio Voice phone line is the Twilio Voice Channel (`util-twilio-channel`) Skill, with its account in the `twilio-voice` credential. Channels (Telegram, Slack, Discord, Twilio Voice) are not connectors. Every OAuth app of your own lists one redirect URI, the same for every vendor: https://api.wiro.ai/v1/AgentConnector/OAuthCallback.

### Credentials

Credentials hold what an agent is, not the services it works with: channels (telegram, slack, discord), twilio-voice, the Wiro project (wiro) and settings (var-support-email, var-website, var-newsletter-test-email). Connectors are on Agent Connectors (see ### Connectors above). A CredentialUpsert row whose `credentialkey` is a connector's slug refuses the whole request before anything is saved: `Unknown credential: <key>. Connectors are connected with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect.` Deploy refuses a connector's slug in `credentials` (`Unknown credential: <key>. Connect a connector after the deploy with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect.`) and a `skills` name that isn't a Skill (`Unknown skill: <name>.`; an `int-*` name: `Unknown skill: <name>. Connectors are connected with UserAgent/ConnectorConnect, not turned on as skills.`), before anything is created or charged.

Wiro project (`wiro`, the project an agent runs models with): `POST /UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind` with the project's id. Connecting the Wiro AI Models (`wiro`) connector binds the project it is given the same way; disconnecting it leaves the project bound, so the agent's Skills keep running models with it.

Values: set via `POST /UserAgent/CredentialUpsert` with `fields[]`. One row per field: `{ credentialkey: "<key>", fieldname: "<field>", fieldvalue: "<value>" }`. Lists (channel allowlists and room lists, Twilio phone numbers, website urls) take the whole list as an array `fieldvalue`, or one entry's field per row with `parentfield` (the list field's key) + `ordinal` (index). Keys and fields: telegram (bottoken, allowedusers JSON array, groups[]), slack (bottoken, apptoken, workspaceid, allowedusers JSON array, channels[]), discord (bottoken, applicationid, allowedusers JSON array, guilds[]), twilio-voice (accountsid, authtoken, phonenumbers[], maxcallseconds, whitelistedcallers[], hold settings), var-website (urls[] of {websitename, url}, both required; the list sent replaces the saved one, and an entry missing either is refused with `Website Name in Websites #1 is required` or `URL in Websites #1 is required`), var-support-email (value), var-newsletter-test-email (value). Communication channels activate from complete required credentials. `directchatmode` is written through `POST /UserAgent/UpdateSettings` or Deploy.

History: `POST /UserAgent/CredentialFieldHistory` lists the value each save replaced, with `operation: "update"`; a first save and a list of entries sent whole (Telegram groups, Slack channels, Discord guilds, Website urls) add no entry, and an encrypted field's earlier values read "[REDACTED]".

## Organizations & Teams

Wiro supports personal and team workspaces. Personal is the default. Organizations group teams; teams hold projects, agents, and wallets.

Context resolution: API key determines context automatically. Team project API key → team context. Personal project API key → personal context. No extra headers needed. A team project's API key works only while the user who created the project is an active member of the team or the organization owner; once the creator is removed, requests with it fail with HTTP 401 "The person who created this API key is no longer in its team. Ask a team admin for a new key." (public endpoints answer as if no key was sent).

Team and organization changes need a signed-in user (dashboard or Bearer token): Organization/Create, Organization/Remove, Organization/Restore, Team/Create, Team/Update, Team/Remove, Team/Member/Invite, Team/Member/CancelInvite, Team/Member/UpdateRole, Team/Member/Remove, Team/TransferAgent, Team/TransferProject and Team/TransferCredit fail with HTTP 401 "API keys can't manage teams or organizations. Sign in and try again." for any API key. Reads (Organization/List, Team/Member/List, SpendLimit/List, SpendLimit/Usage, ModelAccess/List, ModelAccess/Check) work with an API key. Spend limits and Model Access rules are not team settings: SpendLimit/Set, SpendLimit/Remove, SpendLimit/Preview, ModelAccess/Set, ModelAccess/Remove and ModelAccess/Preview work with a personal project's key and with the key of a team project whose creator is a team admin or the organization owner; a key follows its creator's current role, so while its creator is another member it can only read them.

Roles: Owner (org creator: creates/removes teams, edits/removes/restores the org, admin of every team they create and can't be demoted to member), Admin (team settings, the team's spend limits including member limits, the team's Model Access rules, invites, roles, team agents and projects, transfers, coupons, team wallet auto-pay), Member (run models, create projects, chat with team agents, view members, the team's spend limits and Model Access rules, and every member's spending). On a team agent whose Chat Mode is "collaborative", the team's admins and the agent's owner can watch its Screen in the Wiro panel, and an app can show it through a team project's API key that one of them created; other members can't, and nobody can take control of a team agent's computer.

Endpoints:
- POST /Organization/Create: `{ name, description? }` → creates org, caller becomes owner; also creates a "Default Team" with its own wallet and the caller as admin
- POST /Organization/List: returns all orgs with teams, roles, wallet balances
- POST /Organization/Remove: `{ organizationguid }`. Owner only; soft-deletes the org, archives the teams and members that are active at that moment, and cancels pending invites; each project returns to its creator's personal workspace and each agent to its deployer's (with Take Control off until the deployer resets its browser, as for any agent that has been in a team); team wallet balances are not moved
- POST /Organization/Restore: `{ organizationguid }`. Owner only; reactivates the org and only the teams and members that were active when it was deleted (teams and members removed earlier stay removed, invites stay cancelled); projects and agents are not moved back into the teams. Orgs deleted before Wiro recorded this, or whose teams had all been deleted first, fail with "This organization can't be restored automatically because we can't tell which of its teams and members were removed with it. Please contact support."
- POST /Team/Create: `{ organizationguid, name }`. Creates team with own wallet
- POST /Team/Update: `{ teamguid, name?, description? }`. Owner or team admin; spend limits and Model Access rules are set with SpendLimit/Set and ModelAccess/Set
- POST /Team/Remove: `{ teamguid }`. Owner only; soft-deletes the team and removes its members and pending invites; each project returns to its creator's personal workspace (its API key then bills the creator's personal wallet) and each agent to its deployer's (with Take Control off until the deployer resets its browser, as for any agent that has been in a team); the team wallet balance is not moved, so transfer it out first
- POST /Team/Member/Invite: `{ teamguid, email, role? }`. Owner or team admin; emails an invite link that expires after 72 hours; `role` is `"admin"` or `"member"` (default `"member"`); the response, like Team/Member/List, doesn't include the invite token, which only the email carries
- POST /Team/Member/Accept: `{ invitetoken }`. Accepts an invite (the token from the invite link, valid 72 hours); you must be signed in with the invited email address. Without a signed-in account the call fails with "Please sign in or sign up to accept this invitation" (code 98); signed in with a different email, it fails with "This invitation was sent to a different email address"; the organization owner always joins as admin
- POST /Team/Member/CancelInvite: `{ teammemberguid }`. Owner or team admin; cancels a pending invite
- POST /Team/Member/List: `{ teamguid }` → member[] (guid = teammemberguid, role, status, user profile; pending invites included); any team member
- POST /Team/Member/Remove: `{ teammemberguid }`. Owner or team admin; `teammemberguid` is the member's `guid` from Team/Member/List; the team's last admin can't be removed; another admin can't remove the organization owner ("Only the organization owner can remove the owner from this team"), but the owner can remove themselves; the API keys of projects the removed member created stop working unless they are the organization owner
- POST /Team/Member/UpdateRole: `{ teammemberguid, role }`. `role` is `"admin"` or `"member"`; it changes only the role (a member limit is SpendLimit/Set with `scope: "member"` and the member's `useruuid` as `target`); the last admin can't be demoted, and nobody can demote the organization owner ("The organization owner is always an admin of their teams and can't be made a member")
- POST /Team/TransferAgent: `{ useragentguid, targetteamguid }`. Empty string for personal; team side needs team admin or org owner, personal side only the deployer; an agent that has been in a team doesn't get Take Control after it moves back to personal until its owner resets its browser with POST /UserAgent/ResetBrowser (its browser may still hold team members' sign-ins); the answer's `wiroproject` says what happened to the agent's Wiro project: `none` (no project, or a key no project has any more), `kept` (the project is in the new workspace), `cleared` (it isn't, so the project is disconnected and the agent's `wiro` connection deleted; `notes` holds "The agent's Wiro project belongs to another workspace, so the agent was disconnected from it. Pick a project of its new workspace so the agent can run models again.") or `failed` (it isn't and could not be disconnected, so the agent still runs its models with it; `notes` holds "The agent still runs its models with a project of another workspace, so that workspace's spend limits and Model Access rules still apply to it. Check the agent's Wiro project: it should be a project of its new workspace.")
- POST /Team/TransferProject: `{ projectapikey, targetteamguid }`. Empty string for personal; team side needs team admin or org owner, personal side only the creator; the key stops working if its creator is neither an active member of the target team nor the org owner
- POST /Team/TransferCredit: `{ amount, sourceteamguid, targetteamguid }`. Transfer credit between wallets, preserves expiry

Spend limits (https://wiro.ai/docs/spend-limits): one system for every wallet, personal or team; the limits of the call's workspace apply (a team project's key: its team; a personal key: the personal account; the dashboard: the selected workspace). Each limit caps one scope over a period: `account` (the whole wallet; in a team, the whole team), `member` (one team member's spending in the team: their dashboard runs in the team workspace and every run with the key of a team project they created; team wallets only; target = their `useruuid`), `project` (one API key; target = the project `id`), `surface` (one way in, nine targets in this order: `web` = the dashboard and calls with a signed-in user's Bearer token, `api` = calls with an API key, /sync and the self-hosted Wiro MCP npm package before 2.0.0 included, `mcp` = the hosted Wiro MCP server at mcp.wiro.ai and the self-hosted npm package from 2.0.0, which names itself with `x-wiro-client: wiro-mcp/<version>`, `llm-gateway` = the OpenAI and Anthropic compatible LLM gateway at llm.wiro.ai, `extension` = only the Wiro browser extensions, `agent` = your deployed agents (their plan payments, the AI usage their balance pays and their model runs), `studio` = Studio's messages and the models it runs for you, `workflow-agent` = the Workflow Agent's messages, `workflow` = workflow runs, resumes and every step; when work fits several, the first match decides: who does it (Studio, the Workflow Agent, a deployed agent), what it is (a workflow run or resume and the steps it runs, unless one of your deployed agents sends it), which client (the LLM gateway, an extension, MCP), then the credential (an API key: `api`, else `web`); the same surface a task records in `surface`, https://wiro.ai/docs/tasks. Studio and Workflow Agent work used to count on `web` (or `api` with a key) and a workflow run on the surface that started it; limits already set were not changed, so a `web` or `api` limit no longer covers that work) or `agent` (one deployed agent, target = its guid: all of its AI usage, plan-covered and from the balance, and its own model runs; its plan payments count toward the wallet's other limits). `period`: `month` (default; resets on the 1st at 00:00 UTC) or `day` (resets at 00:00 UTC); one monthly and one daily limit per scope and target. `amountusd`: rounded to cents, and at least 0.01 once rounded; a limit counts its whole current period's spending, also from before it was added, so a new limit below that is used up at once. `alertpct`: 50, 80 (default) or 90, or null for no alert email.

What counts: every charge to the wallet for usage (model runs, workflow runs, realtime sessions, Studio, the Workflow Agent, agent plans and upgrades, and an agent's AI usage paid from the balance); deposits are not spending. The models Studio runs for you are checked and counted like your own runs (the account's or team's limits, your member limit, the limit of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's Studio project for a message from wiro.ai), and the `studio` surface's limit); the chat of Studio and the Workflow Agent counts too, on the `studio` and `workflow-agent` surfaces. An agent's AI usage that its plan covers counts only toward the agent's own limit; what the balance pays also counts toward the account's or team's limit and the `agent` surface's limit (never member or API key limits). Checked before work starts: model runs, workflow runs and resumes (with the run's known price) and each workflow step before it starts, Studio and Workflow Agent messages, an agent deploy, upgrade or renewal a person starts, and messages to an agent (its own limit and, once its included usage is used up, the account's or team's and the `agent` surface's). Work in progress: a run that starts holds its expected price against every limit that covers it until it is charged or ends, so runs started at once pass a limit by one run at most; a run with no known price starts while the limit has room; refusals and `heldusd` in List and Usage show what is held. A known price (fixed-price models, workflow runs, agent plans) is refused if spending so far plus what is held plus the price would go over the limit; otherwise work is refused once the limit has no room left. Work already running finishes and is charged, except: a realtime session ends after the turn that uses up a limit and its WebSocket clients get `task_session_stopped` (reason `spend_limit`, code 93, the /Run refusal text); an agent's voice call ends the same way, a web voice call with `session_end` reason `spend_limit` and a phone call after a short spoken notice; and an agent pauses at its next model call when a limit that covers it is used up, even mid-reply. Every agent plan payment (deploy, upgrade, renewal) counts toward the account's or team's limit and the `agent` surface's limit, whichever way it was made, in a team toward the buyer's member limit, and toward the API key's limit when made with one; never toward the agent's own limit. Automatic renewals of agent plans, every 30 days whether or not the agent is running, count the same way, with no API key, and are never refused.

Refusal: HTTP 200, `result: false`, code 93, e.g. `This API key's monthly spend limit is reached ($50.20 of $50.00). It resets on December 1, 2026 at 00:00 UTC.` Subjects: `Your monthly spend limit` (personal account), `This team's monthly spend limit`, `Your monthly spend limit in this team` (member), `This API key's monthly spend limit`, `The monthly spend limit for <label>` (surface labels: the dashboard, the API, MCP, the LLM gateway, the browser extensions, agents, Studio, the Workflow Agent, workflows), `This agent's monthly spend limit`; `daily` for day limits, which end `It resets at 00:00 UTC.` Known-price form: `<Subject> has $L left of $Y, and this run costs $P. It resets ...`. When work in progress holds part of the limit, the message says how much. Nothing runs or is charged; retrying does not help until the limit resets or is raised. Messages to an agent whose own limit is used up are refused with code 93. While it is used up, the agent's Scheduled Tasks pause (not fail) and run at their next scheduled time once it resets, is raised or is removed, with no restart, and Telegram, Slack and Discord users get a plain sentence without the code, with the time the limit resets when that is known.

Emails: an alert at the threshold and a used-up email when the limit is reached, each once per limit and period; changing a limit re-arms both. The emails link to the Spend Limits page of the limit's workspace. Personal: the account. Team: the team's admins and the organization owner, plus the member a member limit is for, the creator of the API key a key limit is for, and the owner of the agent an agent limit is for.

Who changes limits (Set, Remove, Preview): a personal account's owner; in a team, a team admin (the team's creator is one) or the organization owner. Other team members read limits and usage (List, Usage) but can't change any limit, not their own member limit and not the limits of the keys they created or the agents they deployed. A deployed agent's own calls to /SpendLimit are refused with HTTP 403, reads included. Set, Remove and Preview work in the dashboard, with a signed-in user's Bearer token and with an API key. A key acts as the person who created its project, in that project's workspace (the creator's personal account, or the project's team), and follows that person's current role, so while the creator is a member who is not an admin the key is refused like that member. A Bearer call works in the personal account unless it sends the team's guid in `x-team-guid` (API key calls ignore that header); one whose `x-team-guid` names a team the caller is not a member of, in an organization they don't own, gets "You are not a member of this team." List and Preview return `workspace`, to check where a change lands. Changes made with API keys (Set and Remove) are limited to 60 per workspace in any hour, spend limits and Model Access rules together, and Preview does not count (past the cap: "Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later."); each change is recorded with who made it and how. Dashboard: Controls > Spend Limits, https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/spend-limits (personal account or the selected team workspace); team and member limits set before this system were moved into it as monthly limits of the same amount.

Spend limit endpoints (POST, JSON; workspace = the call's own):
- POST /SpendLimit/List: `{}` → `{ result, errors, workspace: { type: "team"|"personal", teamguid, canmanage }, caller: { surface, projectid }, limits: [{ guid, scope, target, targetlabel, period, amountusd, alertpct, periodstart, resetsat, createdat, updatedat, updatedby, spentusd, heldusd }] }`. `canmanage`: whether this caller can change limits here (true for a personal account's owner, a team admin and the organization owner, with their keys too; false for other members and their keys). `caller`: the surface this call counts on and the project id of the calling key (null without a key). `target` is "" for account; `targetlabel` is the member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label (null for account); `spentusd` is this period's spending; `heldusd`, when work in progress holds part of the limit, is how much it holds; `updatedby` is who changed the limit last, `{ useruuid, label }` (label: the person's name, or email without one; `the organization owner` for the owner of the team's organization who is not in the team; null for someone who left the team; a key's change names the key's creator), or null when Wiro did (limits moved into this system); times in Unix seconds. Any member; works with an API key
- POST /SpendLimit/Set: `{ scope, target?, period?, amountusd, alertpct? }` → `{ result, errors, limit }` (a List row). Adds a limit or changes the one with the same scope, target and period (re-arms its emails for the period). Only the people who change limits; signed in or with an API key. `amountusd` at least 0.01. Errors: "scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent.", "Member limits exist only in a team workspace.", "target is required for this scope.", "A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.", "target must be a project id.", "period must be month or day.", "amountusd must be a positive number.", "amountusd is too large." (over 10,000,000), "amountusd must be at least 0.01." (above zero but less than one cent once rounded), "alertpct must be 50, 80 or 90, or null for no alert.", "You are not a member of this team." (Bearer, `x-team-guid` of a team you are not in), "Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit." (signed in, not a team admin or the organization owner), "This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit." (a key whose creator is a member who is not an admin), "That person is not an active member of this team.", "That API key's project is not in this workspace.", "That agent is not in this workspace.", "Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later." (after 60 key changes in the last hour)
- POST /SpendLimit/Preview: the body of Set → `{ result, errors, preview: true, workspace: { type, teamguid, canmanage }, limit, existing }`. Checks the change as Set does, with the same errors and the same people allowed, and changes nothing; it does not count toward the hourly cap on key changes. `limit` is the limit as Set would save it (a List row, with this period's `spentusd`: a new amount at or below it is used up at once; `guid` and `createdat` of the limit it replaces, or null for a new one; `updatedat` and `updatedby` null); `existing` is the current limit with the same scope, target and period, or null
- POST /SpendLimit/Remove: `{ guid }` → `{ result, errors }`. Only the people who change limits; signed in or with an API key. Errors: "guid is required.", "Limit not found in this workspace.", "You are not a member of this team.", "Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.", "This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this limit.", "Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later."
- POST /SpendLimit/Usage: `{ period? }` (`month` default, or `day`) → `{ result, errors, usage: { period, periodstart, resetsat, totalusd, heldusd?, surfaces: [{ surface, label, spentusd, heldusd? }] (one row per surface, all nine in this order: web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow), members: [{ useruuid, label, spentusd, heldusd? }] (empty for a personal account), projects: [{ projectid, label, spentusd, heldusd? }], agents: [{ useragentguid, label, spentusd, heldusd? }] } }`. `heldusd`: what work in progress holds, present only when it holds something; a member, API key or agent whose only spending so far is held work is listed with `spentusd` 0. An agent plan's automatic renewal counts in `totalusd`, in the `agent` surface row and, in a team, under the member who bought the plan, but in no project or agent row. An agent's row counts what its own limit counts, the AI usage its plan covered included. Any member; works with an API key

Model Access (https://wiro.ai/docs/model-access): which models a wallet's work can run, the same way for every wallet, personal or team; the rules of the call's workspace apply (as for spend limits). A rule covers one scope with the spend limits' scopes and targets: `account` (the whole wallet; in a team, every run in the team), `member` (one team member's runs in the team; team wallets only; target = their `useruuid`), `project` (one API key; target = the project `id`), `surface` (`web`, `api`, `mcp`, `llm-gateway`, `extension`, `agent`, `studio`, `workflow-agent` or `workflow`, decided as for spend limits; rules on `web` or `api` set before Studio, the Workflow Agent and workflows had their own surfaces no longer cover that work) or `agent` (one deployed agent: the models it runs through Wiro, the chat models it answers with and its built-in voice; target = its guid). One rule per scope and target. A rule has `access` (Everything Else: `allow`, the default, or `block`, which makes the rule an allowlist), `categories` and `models` (single models by `owner/slug` or id, at most 500, each a model listed on Wiro), each entry `allow` or `block`. Categories (key: label: catalog `categories` values): `image` Image Generation (text-to-image, image-to-image, image-editing, image-to-text), `video` Video Generation (text-to-video, image-to-video, video-to-video, speech-to-video, talking-head, video-to-text, reference-to-video, audio-to-video, lip-sync), `audio` Audio & Speech (text-to-speech, speech-to-text, speech-to-speech, video-to-music, voice-clone, text-to-audio, image-to-audio, realtime-conversation, realtime-tts, realtime-stt), `music` Music Generation (music-generation, text-to-song, text-to-music, image-to-song, image-to-music), `3d` 3D Generation (3d-generation, text-to-3d, image-to-3d), `llm` LLM & Chat (chat, llm, partner-llm, rag, llm-reasoning), `utilities` Utilities (utils); a model can be in several, or in none (then its own entry or Everything Else decides). One rule decides a model by the model's own entry, else its categories (a block among them wins over an allow), else Everything Else. A run goes ahead only when every rule that applies allows the model (account, the member in a team, the API key, the surface, the agent); a narrower rule can't open what a wider one blocks.

Checked before work starts: model runs (/Run and /sync, realtime sessions, the LLM gateway, MCP, the browser extensions, the dashboard), workflow runs and resumes (every model step that will run; steps that will not run, such as those after a breakpoint, are not checked), the models Studio runs for you and the chat model of each message to Studio or the Workflow Agent (your own rules: the account's or team's rule, your member rule, the rule of the turn's project (the API key you sent the message with, or the workspace's Studio project for a message from wiro.ai), and the `studio` surface's rule, `workflow-agent` for a message to the Workflow Agent; a blocked chat model, the `model` sent or the default when none, refuses the message with code 92 before anything runs; chat models are LLM & Chat models, so a rule that blocks LLM & Chat, or lets only selected models run without allowing LLM & Chat, blocks them unless it allows the chat model by name; Studio/Status and StudioWorkflow/Status list the blocked ones), the models deployed agents run through Wiro, an agent's chat model (its settings, or `model` on Message/Send: the agent's own rule, the account's or team's rule and the `agent` surface's rule decide, never member or API key rules; a Scheduled Task whose model a rule blocks pauses instead of failing and runs at its next scheduled time once the model is allowed or another one is chosen), and an agent's built-in voice (voice-note transcription and voice replies, read as Audio & Speech models under the same rules as its chat model; a rule that blocks Audio & Speech, or lets only selected models run without allowing Audio & Speech, blocks them even when it allows LLM & Chat; voice notes then go untranscribed and replies come as text; a Gemini agent's voice notes are transcribed by `google/gemini-3-flash`, so a rule that names that model decides them too; a rule that does not name it blocks those voice notes unless it lets both Audio & Speech and LLM & Chat models run). Catalog browsing (Tool/List, Tool/Detail, the gateway's model list) is not filtered. A change applies to work that starts after it; a deployed agent's chat model and voice follow a change within about a minute.

Refusal: HTTP 200, `result: false`, code 92, naming the rule, e.g. `This API key can only use selected models, and openai/gpt-6-2-astra is not one of them. Model Access rules decide which models can run.` (Everything Else), `This API key can't use openai/gpt-6-2-astra. ...` (the model's entry), `MCP can't use Video Generation models, and bytedance/seedance-v2-5-flash is one of them. ...` (a category). Subjects: `Your account` (personal account rule), `This team`, `You ... in this team` (member), `This API key`, the surface label capitalized (The dashboard, The API, MCP, The LLM gateway, The browser extensions, Agents, Studio, The Workflow Agent, Workflows; e.g. `Studio can't use ...`), `This agent`. When several rules block, the first in the order account, member, API key, surface, agent is named. Nothing runs or is charged; retrying does not help until the rule changes. LLM gateway: HTTP 403 `model_not_allowed`; MCP: a tool error with Wiro's message.

Who changes rules (Set, Remove, Preview): the same people as for spend limits: a personal account's owner; in a team, a team admin or the organization owner. Other team members read rules (List, Check) but can't change any rule, not their own member rule and not the rules of the keys they created or the agents they deployed; a deployed agent's own calls to /ModelAccess are refused with HTTP 403. Set, Remove and Preview work in the dashboard, with a Bearer token (`x-team-guid` picks the team) and with an API key (acting as the person who created the key's project, with that person's current role, in that project's workspace). Changes made with API keys share the spend limits' cap: 60 per workspace in any hour for limits and rules together (Preview does not count); each change is recorded with who made it and how. Dashboard: Controls > Model Access, https://wiro.ai/panel/controls/model-access. Team allowlists and blocklists set before this system were moved into it as rules for the whole team.

Model Access endpoints (POST, JSON; workspace = the call's own):
- POST /ModelAccess/List: `{}` → `{ result, errors, workspace: { type: "team"|"personal", teamguid, canmanage }, caller: { surface, projectid }, rules: [{ guid, scope, target, targetlabel, access, categories: [{ category, label, access }], models: [{ id, model, title, access }], createdat, updatedat, updatedby }], categories: [{ category, label, values }] }`. `target` is "" for account; `targetlabel` is the member's name, the project's name, the agent's title or the surface's label (null for account); `models` in id order, `id` a string, `model` the `owner/slug`; `canmanage`, `caller` and `updatedby` as in SpendLimit/List (`updatedby` null for the team allowlists and blocklists moved into this system); times in Unix seconds. Any member; works with an API key
- POST /ModelAccess/Set: `{ scope, target?, access?, categories?, models? }` → `{ result, errors, rule }` (a List row). `categories`: `[{ category, access }]` or `{ "<category>": access }`; `models`: `[{ model, access }]` or `{ "<owner/slug or id>": access }`. Adds a rule or replaces the one with the same scope and target as a whole. Only the people who change rules; signed in or with an API key. Errors: "scope must be one of account, member, project, surface, agent.", "Member rules exist only in a team workspace.", "target is required for this scope.", "A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.", "target must be a project id.", "access must be allow or block.", "categories must be a list of { category, access }.", "A category is one of image, video, audio, music, 3d, llm, utilities.", "A category's access must be allow or block.", "models must be a list of { model, access }.", "A rule can name at most 500 models.", "Each model needs its owner/slug or id.", "A model's access must be allow or block.", "<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id.", "<model> is not a model on Wiro.", "<model> is named twice.", "You are not a member of this team." (Bearer, `x-team-guid` of a team you are not in), "Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule." (signed in, not a team admin or the organization owner), "This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule." (a key whose creator is a member who is not an admin), "That person is not an active member of this team.", "That API key's project is not in this workspace.", "That agent is not in this workspace.", "Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later." (after 60 key changes in the last hour)
- POST /ModelAccess/Preview: the body of Set → `{ result, errors, preview: true, workspace: { type, teamguid, canmanage }, rule, existing, agentchatmodel }`. Checks the change as Set does, with the same errors and the same people allowed, and changes nothing; it does not count toward the hourly cap on key changes. `rule` is the rule as Set would save it (a List row; `guid` and `createdat` of the rule it replaces, or null for a new one; `updatedat` and `updatedby` null); `existing` is the current rule with the same scope and target, or null; for an agent rule only, `agentchatmodel: { ref, model, blocked }` is the chat model the agent answers with (`ref` as its settings name it, `model` its owner/slug) and whether the rule would block it, which would stop the agent from answering within about a minute of the rule being saved ([MODEL_NOT_ALLOWED])
- POST /ModelAccess/Remove: `{ guid }` → `{ result, errors }`. Only the people who change rules; signed in or with an API key. Errors: "guid is required.", "Rule not found in this workspace.", "You are not a member of this team.", "Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.", "This API key acts as the person who created it, who is a member of this team. Only a team admin or the organization owner can change this rule.", "Too many changes to Spend Limits and Model Access in the last hour. Try again later."
- POST /ModelAccess/Check: `{ model, member?, project?, surface?, agent? }` → `{ result, errors, check: { model, categories, allowed, message, rules: [{ rule, access, by: "model"|"category"|"default", category }], context: { surface, member: { useruuid, label } | null, project: { projectid, label } | null, agent: { useragentguid, label } | null } } }`. How the applicable rules decide one model for one run; nothing runs. Default: a dashboard run (`surface` web) of the caller (with an API key, the person who created its project), or in a team of `member`. `project`: a run made with that project's API key, as the person who created the project; `surface` is api unless named, and web is refused. `agent`: a model run that agent makes, with the API key it runs models with (the Wiro project connected with UserAgent/CredentialProjectBind), as that key's creator, on the agent surface; `project` is not used. With `project` or `agent`, `member` is not used. `check.context` says which run was checked; its `member` is null in a personal account. `message` is the code 92 refusal, or null. Any member; works with an API key. Errors: "model is required.", "<model> is not a model's owner/slug or id.", "<model> is not a model on Wiro.", "A surface is one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.", "Name the agent to check its runs." (surface agent without `agent`), "That API key's project is not in this workspace.", "A run made with an API key never counts as the dashboard. Leave surface out or pick another one." (`project` with surface web), "That agent is not in this workspace.", "That agent has no API key to run models with yet." (no Wiro project connected for the agent), "That agent runs models with an API key of another workspace, so that workspace's rules decide them."

Agent context guards: Message/Send, Message/History, Message/Sessions, Message/DeleteSession, Message/RenameSession, CreateSubscriptionCheckout, PricingPreview, CancelSubscription, RenewSubscription, UpgradeTier and CredentialProjectBind require the request's workspace (the API key's project) to match the agent's; Message/Delete, SkillsApply and SkillToggle require the same for team agents only. Realtime/WebStart checks team agents only too, and also accepts the member who deployed the agent from any workspace while they are still an active member of its team. Realtime/ScreenInfo and Realtime/ScreenStart hold an API key to its own workspace: a team project's key opens only that team's agents (another workspace's agent: code 96 `This API key belongs to another workspace than this agent. Use a key of the agent's own workspace.`), and a personal project's key opens a team agent while its owner is still an active member of the team. A mismatch returns "This agent belongs to a team. Switch to the team context to access it.", "This agent is in your personal workspace. Switch to personal context to access it." or "This agent belongs to a different team." Deploy creates the agent in the key's workspace; with a team key, the key's owner must be a team admin. On a team agent, CreateSubscriptionCheckout, RenewSubscription, CancelSubscription and UpgradeTier are limited to the member who deployed it, team admins and the organization owner (a plan paid by card before agent plans moved to the balance: only a team admin or the organization owner can cancel it); every agent plan is paid from the balance of the agent's workspace (Deploy and CreateSubscriptionCheckout need `useprepaid: true`), a team agent's from the team wallet, which also pays its AI usage past the plan's included usage. A team balance that can't pay a plan: Deploy, CreateSubscriptionCheckout, UpgradeTier and RenewSubscription answer code 97 `The team's balance is $x; this plan needs $y. Add funds to continue.` with `neededusd` and charge nothing (tell it from the team admin refusal by `neededusd`). SkillsApply, SkillToggle and CredentialProjectBind: the member who deployed the agent and team admins. Other members get code 97 "Only a team admin can perform this action on a team-owned agent."

Resource isolation: Project/List, Project/UsageSummary, UserAgent/MyAgents, Task/List, Task/Stat, Wallet/List, Wallet/TransactionList, Coupon/UserList all filter by active context. In team context, Project/List rows carry `apikey` only for projects the caller created, unless the caller is a team admin or the organization owner; other rows carry `apikeymasked` (first and last 4 characters) instead. With an API key, the caller is the user who created the key's project. Project/UsageSummary counts only charges made with one of the workspace's projects (an agent's plan payments and AI usage are not in it) and takes an optional `surface` (web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent or workflow; any other value: `surface must be one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.`); rows from before surfaces were recorded have none, so a surface filter leaves them out.

POST /Wallet/TransactionList: `{ uuid: "me", type: "all" or text a row type contains (such as "payment"), start?, limit? (default 100, max 400), surface?, useragentguid? }` → `{ result, errors, total, wallettransaction }`, the active workspace's wallet rows, newest first. Agent rows (plan payments, AI usage, model runs, funds added from an agent's page) carry `useragentguid`; a charge carries `surface`; an agent's AI usage row carries `usage` `{ model, calls, tokens, costs }` (USD per kind of token; a batch paid more than one way gives a row for each way, each with the whole batch's `usage`). `USAGE (AGENT PLAN)` rows are AI usage an agent's plan covered: they took nothing from the balance, so leave them out of totals (`type: "payment"` lists only the rows that took money from the balance). Unknown surface: `surface must be one of web, api, mcp, llm-gateway, extension, agent, studio, workflow-agent, workflow.` Older rows carry no `surface` or `useragentguid`. One agent's rows in dollars with a monthly summary: POST /UserAgent/TransactionList.

## Links

- [Wiro Platform](https://wiro.ai): Main website
- [Dashboard](https://wiro.ai/panel): Manage projects and API keys
- [Create Project](https://wiro.ai/panel/project/new): Get API key and secret
- [Explore Models](https://wiro.ai/models): Browse all available AI models
- [Full Documentation](https://wiro.ai/docs): Interactive API documentation
- [Full Markdown Export](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wiroai/Wiro-Docs/main/markdown/full-documentation.md): All docs in a single markdown file
- [MCP GitHub](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-MCP): MCP server source code
- [MCP npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp): MCP server package
- [Wiro-Plugin](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Plugin): plugin for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Devin, Antigravity and Kiro, with slash commands and agent skills
- [Wiro-Skills](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Skills): agent skills for images, image edits, video, music, speech, transcripts, 3D and model search, for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot and OpenClaw (`npx skills add wiroai/Wiro-Skills`)
- [Wiro-LLM](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-LLM): Vercel AI SDK provider for chat, images, speech, transcription and video (`@wiro-ai/wiro-llm` on npm)
- [Wiro-Next-Starter](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Next-Starter): Next.js starter with a Playground, image, video and audio tools and LLM chat, for Vercel and Railway
- [Wiro-ComfyUI](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-ComfyUI): ComfyUI nodes for image, video, audio, 3D and LLM models; on the [Comfy Registry](https://registry.comfy.org/nodes/comfyui-wiro)
- [Wiro-Dify-Plugin](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Dify-Plugin): Dify plugins: the LLM gateway and voice models as a model provider, plus media tools
- [Wiro-WordPress](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-WordPress): WordPress plugin for featured images, image edits, alt text, narration and SEO suggestions; on [WordPress.org](https://wordpress.org/plugins/wiro-ai/)
- [Wiro-Obsidian](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Obsidian): Obsidian plugin for images, video, speech, music, transcription and text tools; in [Obsidian community plugins](https://community.obsidian.md/plugins/wiro-ai)
- [Wiro-Figma](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Figma): Figma plugin for images, SVG vectors, image edits and text
- [Wiro-Blender](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Blender): Blender add-on for text to 3D, image to 3D and textures
- [Wiro-Raycast](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Raycast): Raycast extension for image and video generation, LLM chat and model search
- [Wiro-Zed](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Zed): Zed extension for the Wiro MCP server
- [Wiro-Action](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Action): GitHub Action that runs models, workflows and LLM prompts
- [Wiro-Hermes](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Hermes): Hermes Agent plugins: media tools and the LLM gateway as a model provider
- [Wiro-Chromium-Extension](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Chromium-Extension): extension for Chrome, Edge, Opera and Brave; on the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/wiro-ai-tools-for-images/cehkhdmppbnfeahegjjkdhangjelehab), [Microsoft Edge Add-ons](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/wiro-ai-tools-for-images/obkibkhehpojlejdoinhlmoofalgaddg) and the [Naver Whale Store](https://store.whale.naver.com/detail/elgobhnkemhlhfakdmpijbknhehnkgle)
- [Wiro-Firefox-Extension](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Firefox-Extension): add-on for Firefox; on [Firefox Add-ons](https://addons.mozilla.org/firefox/addon/wiro-ai/)
- [Wiro-Safari-Extension](https://github.com/wiroai/Wiro-Safari-Extension): extension for Safari on the Mac
